subject: life-skills
description: Life Skills (CAPS Foundation Phase) consolidated question bank. Grades 1–3 BK&H launch scope; Grade 4 (Intermediate Phase) blocked on source doc. Authored by Claude, awaiting head-of-ed review post-engineering.

LS.L1.BKH.T01.title: Me and my body
LS.L1.BKH.T01.description: Personal details, body parts, hygiene, common communicable diseases.
LS.L1.BKH.T01.recovery_strategy: If the learner is stuck, slow down and let them point to and name body parts on themselves or in a picture. Praise every correct answer to build their confidence. Use audio repetition for hygiene routines.

questions.question: What part of your body do you use to walk?
questions.ruby_prompt: Let's think about how your body helps you move. What part of your body do you use to walk?
questions.expected: Foot
questions.memo: We use our feet to walk and run. Hands hold things, eyes help us see, and ears help us hear.

questions.question: Which body part do you use to smell things?
questions.ruby_prompt: When you smell food cooking or a flower, which body part are you using?
questions.context: Picture: nose, ear, eye, mouth.
questions.expected: Nose
questions.memo: Your nose helps you smell things, like food cooking or flowers in the garden.

questions.question: When you wash your hands, what helps the most?
questions.ruby_prompt: Washing your hands keeps germs away. What helps the most when you wash them?
questions.expected: Soap and water
questions.memo: Soap and water together wash away germs. Water alone does not get rid of them all.

questions.question: Put these handwashing steps in the right order.
questions.ruby_prompt: Let's wash our hands together. Drag the steps into the right order.
questions.expected: Wet hands with water,Rub soap on hands,Rinse the soap off,Dry with a clean cloth
questions.memo: First wet your hands, then add soap and rub, then rinse, then dry. Doing them in order kills the most germs.

questions.question: Which one is a part of your face?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one is a part of your face?
questions.context: Picture: an eye, a knee, an elbow, a toe.
questions.expected: Eye
questions.memo: Eyes are on your face, with your nose, ears and mouth. Knees, elbows and toes are on other parts of your body.

questions.question: If you sneeze into your hand and don't wash it, germs can spread to other people. True or false?
questions.ruby_prompt: Listen to this and tell me if it is true or false. If you sneeze into your hand and don't wash it, germs can spread to other people.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: When you sneeze, germs land on your hand. If you touch a friend or a door, the germs can spread. Always sneeze into a tissue or your elbow.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel sick at school?
questions.ruby_prompt: If your tummy hurts or you feel hot at school, what is the best thing to do?
questions.expected: Tell a teacher
questions.memo: Telling a trusted grown-up at school helps you get the care you need. Teachers can call your family or take you to the school nurse.

questions.question: Sipho has a cold and is coughing. What is the kindest thing he can do to keep his friends safe?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho is coughing because he has a cold. What is the kindest thing he can do?
questions.expected: Cough into his elbow
questions.memo: Coughing into your elbow stops germs from getting on your hands or your friends. It is a kind thing to do when you have a cold.

questions.question: Which one helps your body grow strong?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some choices are good for your body and some are not. Which one helps your body grow strong?
questions.expected: A glass of clean water
questions.memo: Drinking clean water and eating healthy food helps your body grow strong. Too many sweets and skipping meals are not good for you.

questions.question: Tell me one good thing about yourself.
questions.ruby_prompt: Everyone has something special about them. Tell me one good thing about you.
questions.expected: I am kind to my friends
questions.memo: Everyone has something good about them. Maybe you are kind, brave, helpful, funny, or good at running. Saying nice things about yourself is healthy.

questions.question: Which one shows good hygiene?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one shows someone keeping clean and safe?
questions.context: Picture: washing hands with soap, eating without washing, playing in dirt then eating, drinking from a friend's cup.
questions.expected: Washing hands with soap
questions.memo: Washing your hands with soap is good hygiene. The other choices can let germs into your body.

questions.question: What should you brush every morning to look after them?
questions.ruby_prompt: Every morning we look after ourselves. What should you brush every morning?
questions.expected: Hair and teeth
questions.memo: Brushing your teeth keeps them clean and strong. Brushing your hair helps you look tidy and ready for the day.

questions.question: What can happen if you don't wash your hands before eating?
questions.ruby_prompt: Think about your hands. What can happen if you don't wash them before you eat?
questions.expected: Germs can make you sick
questions.memo: Germs on your hands can go into your mouth when you eat. They can give you a sore tummy or a cold.

questions.question: Lerato just came inside from playing in the garden. Her friend asks her to share lunch. What should Lerato do first?
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerato has been playing in the garden. Her friend wants to share lunch. What should Lerato do first?
options: Take the food with dirty hands
Wipe her hands on her uniform
questions.expected: Wash her hands, then eat
questions.memo: Lerato's hands have germs from playing outside. Washing first stops the germs from getting onto her food and into her body.

questions.question: Name one disease that you can catch from someone else.
questions.ruby_prompt: Some sicknesses pass from one person to another. Name one you know.
questions.expected: A cold
questions.memo: Diseases like a cold, the flu, and chickenpox can spread from one person to another. We can stop them by washing hands and not sharing cups.

LS.L1.BKH.T02.title: My school
LS.L1.BKH.T02.description: Classroom layout, routines, rules, school structure, evacuation signals, safety.
LS.L1.BKH.T02.recovery_strategy: If the learner is unsure about school routines, walk them through their own school day in order — arrival, classroom, break, lunch, going home. Use the school's actual layout as the teaching tool.

questions.question: Where does the teacher usually stand when teaching the class?
questions.ruby_prompt: Think about your classroom. Where does the teacher usually stand when teaching?
options: At the front of the class
questions.expected: At the front of the class
questions.memo: The teacher stands at the front so everyone can see and hear them. That is where the board is too.

questions.question: What do we do when the teacher says 'Quiet please'?
questions.ruby_prompt: Imagine the teacher says 'Quiet please.' What should we do?
questions.expected: Stop talking and listen
questions.memo: When the teacher asks for quiet, it is so everyone can hear what comes next. Listening is a way of showing respect.

questions.question: Which one is the playground?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at these places. Which one is the playground at your school?
questions.context: Picture: an open grassy area with swings, classroom desks, library shelves, principal's office.
questions.expected: Open grassy area with swings
questions.memo: The playground is where we play and run during break. The other places have different uses.

questions.question: It is okay to push another learner in the line.
questions.ruby_prompt: Listen carefully. Is this true or false? It is okay to push another learner in the line.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Pushing can hurt someone. In school we line up by standing quietly and waiting our turn.

questions.question: What sound at school usually means it is time to go inside?
questions.ruby_prompt: Schools have signals. What sound usually tells us it is time to go inside?
questions.expected: A bell or whistle
questions.memo: A bell or whistle is a signal that everyone can hear. It tells us break is over and lessons start again.

questions.question: If you don't know where the toilet is, who should you ask?
questions.ruby_prompt: You are new and need the toilet. Who is the best person to ask?
options: A teacher or older learner you trust
questions.expected: A teacher or older learner you trust
questions.memo: Trusted school people will help you find your way. It is always okay to ask a teacher.

questions.question: What is a fire drill?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sometimes the school does a fire drill. What is that?
options: A practice to leave the building safely
questions.expected: A practice to leave the building safely
questions.memo: A fire drill teaches us how to get out of the building quickly and quietly if there ever is a real fire. We practise so we know what to do.

questions.question: Put these morning steps at school in the right order.
questions.ruby_prompt: Let's go through morning at school. Drag these into the right order.
questions.expected: Greet the teacher,Hang up your bag,Sit at your desk,Open your workbook
questions.memo: A good morning at school starts with greeting your teacher, then putting your bag away, finding your seat, and getting ready to learn.

questions.question: Who helps to keep your school clean?
questions.ruby_prompt: Many people help at school. Who keeps the school clean?
options: The cleaner and all of us together
questions.expected: The cleaner and all of us together
questions.memo: The cleaner does a lot of the work, but everyone helps by picking up their own litter and looking after the desks and toilets.

questions.question: Tell me one rule in your classroom and why it matters.
questions.ruby_prompt: Class rules help us learn. Tell me one rule in your class and why it matters.
questions.expected: Raise my hand to speak so the teacher can hear one person at a time.
questions.memo: Class rules help everyone learn safely. Saying why a rule matters shows you understand what it is for.

questions.question: If you fall and hurt yourself at school, what should you do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Imagine you trip on the playground and graze your knee. What should you do?
questions.expected: Tell a teacher straight away
questions.memo: A teacher can help clean and cover the cut so it doesn't get worse. Trying to hide a hurt only makes it harder to heal.

questions.question: Which one is a classroom?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at these places. Which one is a classroom?
questions.context: Picture: desks facing a board, a swimming pool, a kitchen, a market.
questions.expected: Desks facing a board
questions.memo: A classroom has desks and a board where the teacher writes. The other places are for swimming, cooking and shopping.

questions.question: What is the principal's main job?
questions.ruby_prompt: Every school has a principal. What is their main job?
questions.expected: To lead the school
questions.memo: The principal looks after the whole school — teachers, learners, and the building. They make sure school runs well.

questions.question: Lerato sees a younger child crying near the gate. What is the kindest thing to do?
questions.ruby_prompt: A small child is crying alone near the school gate. What would be the kindest thing to do?
options: Ask if they are okay and find a teacher to help
questions.expected: Ask if they are okay and find a teacher to help
questions.memo: Asking 'Are you okay?' is a kind first step. A teacher can find out what is wrong and call their family.

questions.question: We should always run inside the school building.
questions.ruby_prompt: Is this true or false? We should always run inside the school building.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Running inside can cause people to bump into each other and get hurt. We walk inside the building and run on the playground.

LS.L1.BKH.T03.title: My family
LS.L1.BKH.T03.description: Family members, roles, family tree, safe/unsafe situations at home, emergency contacts.
LS.L1.BKH.T03.recovery_strategy: If a learner is unsure, draw a simple family tree with them using whoever is in their household. Every family looks different and that is okay. Reinforce that family is the people who care for you.

questions.question: What do we call the child of your mother's brother?
questions.ruby_prompt: Family has special names. What do we call the child of your mother's brother?
questions.expected: Your cousin
questions.memo: Your cousin is the child of your aunt or uncle. They are part of your wider family.

questions.question: Which one is part of your immediate family?
questions.ruby_prompt: Your immediate family is the people closest to you. Which one of these is part of your immediate family?
questions.expected: Your sister
questions.memo: Your immediate family is usually your parents and your brothers and sisters. Other people may be important too, but they are not your immediate family.

questions.question: What is a grandparent?
questions.ruby_prompt: Grandparents are special people. Who is your grandparent?
questions.expected: Your parent's parent
questions.memo: A grandparent is the parent of your mother or father. Some children call them Gogo, Khulu, Ouma, Oupa, or other special names.

questions.question: Which picture shows a family tree?
questions.ruby_prompt: A family tree shows how family members are connected. Which picture shows a family tree?
questions.context: Picture: a drawing with grandparents at the top, parents in the middle, children below; a real tree in a forest; a school building; a car.
options: Drawing with grandparents at top and children below
questions.expected: Drawing with grandparents at top and children below
questions.memo: A family tree is a drawing that shows how people in a family are related, with the oldest people at the top.

questions.question: Every family looks the same.
questions.ruby_prompt: Is this true or false? Every family looks exactly the same.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Families come in many shapes. Some have two parents, some have one, some live with grandparents, aunts, or uncles. All families are families.

questions.question: Who do you call in South Africa if there is a fire?
questions.ruby_prompt: If there is a fire at home and you need help, what should you do?
options: A trusted grown-up, who will call 10177 or the fire department
questions.expected: A trusted grown-up, who will call 10177 or the fire department
questions.memo: Tell a grown-up straight away. In South Africa, 10177 is the emergency number for an ambulance, and fire departments have their own number too.

questions.question: If you cut yourself with a knife at home, what should you do first?
questions.ruby_prompt: You cut your finger by accident. What should you do first?
options: Find a grown-up to help straight away
questions.expected: Find a grown-up to help straight away
questions.memo: A grown-up can clean the cut and put a plaster on it. Hiding it can make it worse and dirty water can make it sore.

questions.question: Which one in the kitchen is dangerous to touch when no grown-up is there?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the kitchen pictures. Which one should you not touch on your own?
questions.context: Picture: a hot stove, a chair, a tea towel, a fruit bowl.
questions.expected: Hot stove
questions.memo: A hot stove can burn you very badly. Only grown-ups should use the stove.

questions.question: Mama has popped to the spaza shop. The doorbell rings and you don't know the person at the door. What should you do?
questions.ruby_prompt: You're at home alone for a short while. The doorbell rings and you don't know who is there. What should you do?
options: Do not open the door — wait for Mama
Give them money through the gate
questions.expected: Do not open the door — wait for Mama
questions.memo: When you are alone at home, never open the door to someone you don't know. Wait for a trusted grown-up to be home.

questions.question: Name one person in your family.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me about your family. Name one person in your family.
questions.expected: My mother
questions.memo: Family members can be parents, brothers, sisters, grandparents, aunties, uncles, or cousins. There is no wrong answer.

questions.question: What is the South African emergency number for an ambulance?
questions.ruby_prompt: If someone in your family is very sick, what number does a grown-up call for an ambulance?
questions.memo: In South Africa, 10177 brings an ambulance. It is good for everyone in the family to know this number.

questions.question: Who is responsible for keeping the family safe and fed at home?
questions.ruby_prompt: Think about your home. Who keeps the family safe and fed?
questions.expected: Grown-ups in the family
questions.memo: Grown-ups look after the family. Children can help with small jobs, but the grown-ups are responsible.

questions.question: It is safe for children to play with matches at home.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? It is safe for children to play with matches at home.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Matches can start fires that hurt people and burn down homes. Only grown-ups should use matches.

questions.question: You smell smoke and see flames in another room at home. What should you do first?
questions.ruby_prompt: You smell smoke and see flames in another room. What is the very first thing you should do?
options: Call out to a grown-up and go outside
Take a video on your phone
Throw water on it by yourself
questions.expected: Call out to a grown-up and go outside
questions.memo: Getting outside and calling a grown-up keeps you safe. Hiding makes it hard for people to find you, and throwing water on the wrong fire can make it worse.

questions.question: Why is it useful to know your home address?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some children know exactly where they live. Why is that useful?
questions.expected: So that grown-ups can help me find my way home or send help if I am lost
questions.memo: Knowing your address means a trusted grown-up can help you home, or call for help to come to you, if you are ever lost.

LS.L1.BKH.T04.title: Ways of travelling
LS.L1.BKH.T04.description: Modes of transport, common road signs, crossing safely, rules in moving vehicles.
LS.L1.BKH.T04.recovery_strategy: Walk a struggling learner through their daily journey to school. Talk about every place they cross a road or get into a vehicle. Road safety improves with practice, so repeat the steps each time.

questions.question: Which one is a vehicle?
questions.ruby_prompt: Vehicles are things that take us from one place to another. Which one is a vehicle?
questions.expected: A car
questions.memo: A car is a vehicle. Pencils, books and flowers are not vehicles — they don't move people from place to place.

questions.question: Which one is a bicycle?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one is a bicycle?
questions.context: Picture: bicycle with two wheels and a handlebar, a chair, a bowl of pap, a hat.
questions.expected: Bicycle with two wheels
questions.memo: A bicycle has two wheels and a handlebar. You can ride it to get around.

questions.question: What does a red traffic light tell drivers to do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Traffic lights tell drivers what to do. What does a red light mean?
questions.expected: Stop
questions.memo: Red means stop. Green means go. Yellow means slow down because it will soon be red.

questions.question: When is it safe to cross the road?
questions.ruby_prompt: Crossing the road can be dangerous. When is it safe to cross?
options: When the cars have stopped and you have looked both ways
questions.expected: When the cars have stopped and you have looked both ways
questions.memo: We only cross when it is safe — that means looking both ways and only stepping out when cars have stopped.

questions.question: A Scholar Patrol is there to help children cross the road safely.
questions.ruby_prompt: Is this true or false? A Scholar Patrol helps children cross the road safely.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Scholar Patrols stop the traffic so children can cross safely on their way to and from school.

questions.question: What does a Stop sign look like?
questions.ruby_prompt: Stop signs help keep us safe. What does a Stop sign look like?
options: A red sign with the word STOP
questions.expected: A red sign with the word STOP
questions.memo: A Stop sign is red and has the word STOP in big white letters. Drivers must stop completely when they see one.

questions.question: Put these crossing-the-road steps in the right order.
questions.ruby_prompt: Let's cross the road safely. Drag the steps into the right order.
questions.expected: Stop at the kerb,Look left and right,Listen for traffic,Cross when it is safe
questions.memo: Stop, look, listen, then cross. Doing these in order every time keeps you safe near roads.

questions.question: When you are in a taxi or a car, what should you do?
questions.ruby_prompt: You're sitting in a taxi or car. What is the safe thing to do?
options: Sit still and wear a seatbelt if there is one
Open the door while it's moving
questions.expected: Sit still and wear a seatbelt if there is one
questions.memo: Staying in your seat keeps you safe if the driver has to stop suddenly. Seatbelts hold you in place.

questions.question: Name one way you can travel to school.
questions.ruby_prompt: There are many ways to get to school. Tell me one.
questions.expected: By walking
questions.memo: We travel to school by walking, taking a taxi, riding a bike, or going in a car or bus. All ways are fine as long as we are safe.

questions.question: You are walking home and a stranger in a car asks you to come closer. What should you do?
questions.ruby_prompt: A stranger in a car calls you over while you walk home. What is the safest thing to do?
options: Walk away quickly and tell a trusted grown-up
questions.expected: Walk away quickly and tell a trusted grown-up
questions.memo: Strangers should not be calling children over. Walking away and telling a trusted grown-up keeps you safe.

questions.question: Which one has wings and flies through the sky?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some vehicles travel through the air. Which one has wings and flies?
questions.expected: An aeroplane
questions.memo: An aeroplane has wings and flies high in the sky. The others travel on the ground.

questions.question: Why must we cross at traffic lights or Scholar Patrol crossings?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is it important to cross only at the right places, like traffic lights or Scholar Patrol?
options: These are the safest places to cross
questions.expected: These are the safest places to cross
questions.memo: Traffic lights and Scholar Patrols are made for crossing. Drivers expect to stop there, so they are the safest places.

questions.question: Which one is a traffic light?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one is a traffic light?
questions.context: Picture: a tall pole with red, yellow and green lights; a flag; a tree; a phone booth.
options: Tall pole with red, yellow and green lights
questions.expected: Tall pole with red, yellow and green lights
questions.memo: A traffic light has red, yellow and green lights stacked on top of each other. It tells drivers when to stop and go.

questions.question: Sipho is late for school and the pedestrian light is still red. What should he do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho is late. The pedestrian light is red. What should he do?
options: Wait for the green walking sign even if he is late
questions.expected: Wait for the green walking sign even if he is late
questions.memo: Being safe is more important than being on time. Cars don't expect people to cross when the light is red — running across is very dangerous.

questions.question: It is safe to play in the road.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? It is safe to play in the road.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Roads have cars, taxis and bicycles moving on them. We play in a safe place away from the road, like a yard or a park.

LS.L1.BKH.T05.title: Food and nutrition
LS.L1.BKH.T05.description: Food preferences, plant growth, food groups, water intake, nutritious choices, traditional foods.
LS.L1.BKH.T05.recovery_strategy: If a learner is stuck, link new content to foods they actually eat at home. Reinforce that there is no single 'right' diet — variety and clean water are the keys.

questions.question: Which one is a healthy snack?
questions.ruby_prompt: Let's choose a healthy snack. Which one is best for your body?
questions.expected: An apple
questions.memo: Fruit like apples gives your body vitamins. Chips, fizzy drinks and sweets have too much salt or sugar.

questions.question: Which one is a vegetable?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one is a vegetable?
questions.context: Picture: a carrot, a sweet, a biscuit, a piece of cake.
questions.expected: A carrot
questions.memo: Carrots are vegetables that grow in the ground. Sweets, biscuits and cake are treats, not vegetables.

questions.question: Put the stages of a growing bean plant in order.
questions.ruby_prompt: Let's watch a bean grow. Drag the stages into the right order.
questions.expected: Seed in the soil,Small green shoot,Bigger plant with leaves,Plant with bean pods
questions.memo: First the seed sits in the soil. Then a small green shoot pushes up. The plant grows leaves, and finally it makes beans we can eat.

questions.question: Why do we need to drink water every day?
questions.ruby_prompt: Water is so important. Why do we drink it every day?
questions.expected: It keeps our body healthy
questions.memo: Our bodies need water to work properly. Drinking clean water every day keeps us healthy and helps our brain think well.

questions.question: Which food group does maize belong to?
questions.ruby_prompt: Maize is a food many of us eat. Which food group does it belong to?
questions.expected: Grains and cereals
questions.memo: Maize, rice, bread and pap are grains. They give our bodies energy to play and learn.

questions.question: Name one traditional South African food.
questions.ruby_prompt: South Africa has many lovely traditional foods. Name one you know.
questions.expected: Pap
questions.memo: Traditional South African foods include pap, samp, biltong, morogo, bunny chow and many more. Every family may have favourites.

questions.question: Which drink is best for your body every day?
questions.ruby_prompt: Of all the drinks, which one is best for your body every single day?
questions.expected: Clean water
questions.memo: Water is the best daily drink. Other drinks can be nice sometimes, but too much sugar is not good for your body or teeth.

questions.question: Eating only sweets every day is good for you.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Eating only sweets every day is good for you.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Sweets every day are not good. They have a lot of sugar that can hurt our teeth and our body needs many different foods to grow.

questions.question: Which one is a fruit?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one is a fruit?
questions.context: Picture: a banana, a potato, a carrot, a slice of bread.
questions.expected: A banana
questions.memo: Bananas grow on trees and are fruit. Potatoes and carrots grow in the ground as vegetables. Bread is made from grain.

questions.question: Why is it important to wash fruit before eating it?
questions.ruby_prompt: Before we eat fruit, we wash it. Why?
questions.expected: To remove dirt and germs
questions.memo: Fruit is often picked from gardens and trees, so it can have dirt and germs on it. Washing with clean water keeps us safe.

questions.question: What does a plant need to grow?
questions.ruby_prompt: Plants need certain things to grow well. What are they?
questions.expected: Water, sunlight and soil
questions.memo: Plants need water to drink, sunlight to make food, and soil for their roots. With all three, they grow strong.

questions.question: Tell me one healthy food you like to eat.
questions.ruby_prompt: Healthy foods make our bodies happy. Tell me one healthy food you like.
questions.expected: An apple
questions.memo: Healthy foods include fruit, vegetables, beans, fish, and whole grains. Everyone has a favourite — there is no wrong answer.

questions.question: Where does milk come from?
questions.ruby_prompt: Milk is in many of our drinks and foods. Where does it come from?
options: Cows and other animals like goats
questions.expected: Cows and other animals like goats
questions.memo: Most of the milk we drink comes from cows. Some people drink goat's milk too. Factories pack it into bottles, but it starts with animals.

questions.question: Lerato's mum is packing a healthy lunchbox. What should she put in it?
questions.ruby_prompt: Help Lerato's mum pack a healthy lunchbox. What should she put in?
options: A sandwich, a fruit, and water
questions.expected: A sandwich, a fruit, and water
questions.memo: A healthy lunchbox has a mix — a sandwich for energy, fruit for vitamins, and water to drink. That keeps Lerato strong for the day.

questions.question: Eating too many sweets can make our teeth sore.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Eating too many sweets can make our teeth sore.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Sugar from sweets can damage our teeth and cause toothache. Brushing helps, but the best plan is to eat sweets only sometimes.

LS.L1.BKH.T06.title: Domestic animals
LS.L1.BKH.T06.description: Pets vs farm animals, care for animals, products from animals (dairy etc).
LS.L1.BKH.T06.recovery_strategy: Connect the lesson to animals the learner has seen — a dog at home, chickens at granny's, cows on a farm trip. Real examples beat abstract lists.

questions.question: Which one is most often a pet?
questions.ruby_prompt: Pets live with people at home. Which one is most often a pet?
questions.expected: A dog
questions.memo: Dogs are common pets in many South African homes. Lions, elephants and sharks are wild animals — they do not live in our houses.

questions.question: Which is a farm animal?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one is a farm animal?
questions.context: Picture: a cow, a tiger, a gecko, a whale.
questions.expected: A cow
questions.memo: Cows live on farms. Tigers and whales are wild animals, and geckos are small lizards that live around buildings.

questions.question: How should you look after a pet dog?
questions.ruby_prompt: If you have a pet dog at home, how do you look after it?
options: Give it food, water and exercise
Let it run on the road alone
questions.expected: Give it food, water and exercise
questions.memo: A pet needs food every day, clean water, and time to play. Looking after a pet teaches us kindness and responsibility.

questions.question: What do chickens give us?
questions.ruby_prompt: Chickens are useful farm animals. What do they give us?
questions.expected: Eggs
questions.memo: Chickens lay eggs that we can eat. Cows give us milk and beef, and sheep give us wool.

questions.question: What do cows give us?
questions.ruby_prompt: Cows are very useful animals. What do they give us?
questions.expected: Milk and meat
questions.memo: Cows give us milk to drink and meat to eat. Wool comes from sheep, eggs from chickens, and honey from bees.

questions.question: Put the steps of milk reaching your cup in order.
questions.ruby_prompt: How does milk get from a cow to your cup? Drag the steps into order.
options: Milk goes into a bottle or carton
questions.expected: Cow eats grass,Farmer milks the cow,Milk goes into a bottle or carton,You drink the milk
questions.memo: The cow eats grass to make milk in her body. The farmer collects it, the factory packs it, and you drink it.

questions.question: Pets live with people at home.
questions.ruby_prompt: Is this true or false? Pets live with people at home.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Pets like dogs, cats, and budgies live at home with their families. The family looks after them and they bring joy.

questions.question: What does a sheep give us?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sheep are common in many parts of South Africa. What do they give us?
questions.expected: Wool and meat
questions.memo: Sheep give us wool to make warm jerseys and blankets, and meat (lamb and mutton).

questions.question: Name one difference between a pet and a farm animal.
questions.ruby_prompt: Pets and farm animals are not exactly the same. Name one way they are different.
questions.expected: Pets live at home with people, farm animals live on a farm and give us food
questions.memo: Pets live with us at home and we look after them as friends. Farm animals usually live on a farm and give us food, milk, eggs or wool.

questions.question: Which animal lives on a farm?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one lives on a farm?
questions.context: Picture: a pig, a fish, a monkey, a snake.
questions.expected: A pig
questions.memo: Pigs are common farm animals. Fish live in water, monkeys live in trees, and snakes are wild animals.

questions.question: Why is milk good for children?
questions.ruby_prompt: Children often drink milk. Why is it good for them?
questions.expected: It helps build strong bones
questions.memo: Milk has calcium, which helps your bones and teeth grow strong. That is why grown-ups often give it to children.

questions.question: How should you treat a pet?
questions.ruby_prompt: Pets feel things, just like us. How should you treat a pet?
questions.expected: With kindness and gentle hands
questions.memo: Pets are living animals with feelings. Treating them kindly keeps them and you safe and happy.

questions.question: Sipho's family farm has a goat with a sore leg. What should they do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho sees that one of the family goats is limping. What should the family do?
options: Call the vet or animal nurse
questions.expected: Call the vet or animal nurse
questions.memo: A vet is an animal doctor. When a farm animal is hurt, a vet can help it get better.

questions.question: Cows can fly in the sky.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Cows can fly in the sky.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Cows cannot fly. They are heavy animals that walk on four legs on the ground. Only birds and bats fly naturally.

questions.question: Name one food or drink we get from animals.
questions.ruby_prompt: Many of our foods come from animals. Name one.
questions.expected: Milk
questions.memo: We get milk from cows, eggs from chickens, meat from many animals, and honey from bees. There are lots of right answers.

LS.L1.BKH.T07.title: Stories of heroes
LS.L1.BKH.T07.description: Important people in SA history, qualities of a hero, basic rescue skills.
LS.L1.BKH.T07.recovery_strategy: Use real local heroes the learner can connect to — a grandparent, a community helper, or someone from their own life. Heroism is about kind, brave actions, not fame.

questions.question: What is a hero?
questions.ruby_prompt: We hear the word hero a lot. What is a hero?
questions.expected: Someone who helps others bravely
questions.memo: A hero is someone who is brave and kind, who helps others even when it is hard. Anyone can be a hero with their actions.

questions.question: Nelson Mandela was a hero because he...
questions.ruby_prompt: Nelson Mandela is one of South Africa's most famous heroes. Why was he a hero?
options: Fought for fairness for all people
Only liked one group of people
questions.expected: Fought for fairness for all people
questions.memo: Nelson Mandela worked his whole life for a fair South Africa where all people are treated equally. That is why we remember him.

questions.question: Which picture shows brave behaviour?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one shows someone being brave?
questions.context: Picture: a child helping someone who fell, a child walking past, a child laughing at someone, a child hiding.
options: A child helping someone who fell
questions.expected: A child helping someone who fell
questions.memo: Stopping to help when someone is hurt takes courage. Walking past or laughing is not brave.

questions.question: Which is a quality of a hero?
questions.ruby_prompt: Heroes share some qualities. Which one is a hero's quality?
questions.expected: Kindness and bravery
questions.memo: Heroes are kind, brave, and think of others. These qualities help them do good things even when it's hard.

questions.question: A child sees a friend fall into a pool. Put the steps in order.
questions.ruby_prompt: If you saw a friend fall into a pool, what should you do? Drag the steps in order.
options: Wait for the grown-up to pull them out
questions.expected: See your friend fall,Shout for a grown-up,Throw something they can hold,Wait for the grown-up to pull them out
questions.memo: Brave helpers don't jump into deep water alone. Shouting for a grown-up is the first and bravest thing to do.

questions.question: Name one hero you have heard of.
questions.ruby_prompt: Heroes can come from history, your family, or even your school. Name one you have heard of.
questions.expected: Nelson Mandela
questions.memo: Heroes include leaders like Nelson Mandela, community helpers, family elders, and even teachers. Any kind, brave person counts.

questions.question: Heroes do good things to help others.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Heroes do good things to help others.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — the most important thing about a hero is that they help others, not just themselves.

questions.question: If you see someone get hurt and they need help, what should you do?
questions.ruby_prompt: You see someone fall and they need help. What is the best thing to do?
questions.expected: Call a grown-up straight away
questions.memo: Calling a grown-up is the best help you can give. Grown-ups know what to do, and you can be a hero by getting them quickly.

questions.question: What makes someone a community hero?
questions.ruby_prompt: We call some people 'community heroes'. What does that mean?
options: They do kind, helpful things for people around them
questions.expected: They do kind, helpful things for people around them
questions.memo: A community hero is anyone who helps their neighbours and community in small or big ways. Heroes are not always famous.

questions.question: Were there only men as heroes in South Africa?
questions.ruby_prompt: South Africa has had many heroes. Were they all men?
options: No — women and men have both been heroes
questions.expected: No — women and men have both been heroes
questions.memo: South African heroes include leaders like Albertina Sisulu and many others. Heroes can be men, women, or children.

questions.question: Which picture shows kindness?
questions.ruby_prompt: Kindness is a hero's quality. Which picture shows kindness?
questions.context: Picture: one child sharing food with another, one child taking a toy from a friend, one child ignoring a sad child, one child shouting.
options: Taking a toy from a friend
questions.expected: Sharing food with another child
questions.memo: Sharing is a kind, hero-like action. The other choices are not kind.

questions.question: Tell me one brave or kind thing someone in your family or community has done.
questions.ruby_prompt: There are everyday heroes around us. Tell me one brave or kind thing someone in your family or community has done.
questions.expected: My grandmother walked far to help a neighbour
questions.memo: Real-life heroes do things like helping a neighbour, looking after a sick relative, or standing up for someone. Any answer counts.

questions.question: What is a basic rescue skill children can use?
questions.ruby_prompt: Children can be heroes too. What is one basic rescue skill you can use?
questions.expected: Shouting loudly for a grown-up
questions.memo: Children shouldn't try to do dangerous rescues alone. Shouting for a grown-up is the safest, most heroic thing.

questions.question: Only famous people can be heroes.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Only famous people can be heroes.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Anyone can be a hero by being kind and brave — your mum, a teacher, an older sibling, even you.

questions.question: Why do we tell stories about heroes?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why do we tell each other stories about heroes?
options: So we can learn from their kindness and bravery
questions.expected: So we can learn from their kindness and bravery
questions.memo: Hearing about heroes teaches us how to be brave and kind too. Their stories help us decide who we want to be.

LS.L1.BKH.T08.title: People who help us
LS.L1.BKH.T08.description: Community helpers and their roles, emergency numbers.
LS.L1.BKH.T08.recovery_strategy: Link helpers to learners' real lives — the nurse at the local clinic, the police officer near school, the teacher in the next class. Helpers are real people, not just pictures.

questions.question: Who do we call when there is a fire?
questions.ruby_prompt: If there is a fire, who do we call to put it out?
questions.expected: The fire department
questions.memo: Firefighters from the fire department are trained to put out fires safely. A trusted grown-up will call them.

questions.question: Which person is a nurse?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which person is a nurse?
questions.context: Picture: a person in scrubs with a stethoscope, a person reading a book, a footballer with a ball, a chef with a pan.
options: The person in scrubs with a stethoscope
questions.expected: The person in scrubs with a stethoscope
questions.memo: Nurses often wear scrubs (special uniforms) and use stethoscopes to listen to your heartbeat. They help people who are sick or hurt.

questions.question: What does a doctor do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Doctors are very important helpers. What do they do?
options: Helps people get better when they are sick
questions.expected: Helps people get better when they are sick
questions.memo: Doctors are trained to find out what is making us sick and help us feel better with medicine or treatment.

questions.question: Who teaches you at school?
questions.ruby_prompt: At school, who is the helper who teaches you?
questions.expected: Your teacher
questions.memo: Teachers are the helpers who teach us reading, writing, maths and many other things at school.

questions.question: What number do you call in South Africa for an ambulance?
questions.ruby_prompt: If someone is very sick or hurt, what number do grown-ups call for an ambulance?
questions.memo: In South Africa, 10177 is the emergency number for an ambulance. It is a good number for everyone in the family to know.

questions.question: Which person helps you cross the road at school?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Who helps you cross the road safely on the way to school?
questions.context: Picture: a scholar patrol with a flag, a chef, a dancer, a doctor.
options: The scholar patrol with a flag
questions.expected: The scholar patrol with a flag
questions.memo: Scholar Patrols stop the traffic so children can cross safely. They are usually older learners trained to do this important job.

questions.question: Police help keep us safe.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Police help keep us safe.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — police officers help keep our communities safe and we can ask them for help if we are lost or in trouble.

questions.question: What does a firefighter do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Firefighters are brave helpers. What do they do?
questions.expected: Puts out fires
questions.memo: Firefighters wear special clothes and use water and equipment to put out fires and rescue people.

questions.question: Tell me about a time someone in the community helped you.
questions.ruby_prompt: Helpers are all around us. Tell me about a time someone in the community helped you.
questions.expected: My teacher helped me when I was lost
questions.memo: Any kind helper counts — a teacher, neighbour, scholar patrol, shopkeeper, anyone who was good to you.

questions.question: Where does a doctor usually work?
questions.ruby_prompt: When you visit a doctor, where do you usually find them?
questions.expected: At a clinic or hospital
questions.memo: Most doctors work at clinics or hospitals where they have everything they need to help sick people.

questions.question: Who builds houses for people?
questions.ruby_prompt: Houses don't build themselves. Who does that work?
questions.expected: A builder
questions.memo: Builders use bricks, cement and tools to build houses, schools and shops where we live, learn and shop.

questions.question: Which person delivers letters and parcels?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Who delivers letters and parcels?
questions.context: Picture: a postal worker with a bag of letters, a chef, a vet, a dancer.
options: The postal worker with a bag of letters
questions.expected: The postal worker with a bag of letters
questions.memo: Postal workers deliver letters and parcels from one place to another. They help families stay in touch.

questions.question: If you are lost in town, who is the safest person to ask for help?
questions.ruby_prompt: You're in town and you can't find your family. Who is the safest helper to ask?
options: A police officer or a shop helper in uniform
questions.expected: A police officer or a shop helper in uniform
questions.memo: People in uniform working at shops or for the police are known helpers. Strangers calling you over are not safe.

questions.question: Bakers make sandwiches at the post office.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Bakers make sandwiches at the post office.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Bakers bake bread and cakes — usually at a bakery, not at the post office.

questions.question: Name one helper in your community.
questions.ruby_prompt: Many helpers live around you. Name one of them.
questions.expected: My teacher
questions.memo: Helpers include teachers, nurses, doctors, police, firefighters, postal workers, shopkeepers, neighbours and many more.

LS.L1.BKH.T09.title: Familiar places (my village / town / city / neighbourhood)
LS.L1.BKH.T09.description: Places close to home and school, important buildings, parks, sporting facilities.
LS.L1.BKH.T09.recovery_strategy: Use the learner's actual neighbourhood as the teaching tool. Ask 'what is near your home?' before moving to bigger places like cities. Familiarity builds confidence.

questions.question: Where do you go to buy food?
questions.ruby_prompt: When the family needs food, where do they go?
questions.expected: A shop, spaza or market
questions.memo: Shops, spaza shops and markets are where people buy food and other things they need every day.

questions.question: Which one is a park?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one is a park?
questions.context: Picture: an open green space with swings and trees, a kitchen, a library, a phone shop.
options: Open green space with swings and trees
questions.expected: Open green space with swings and trees
questions.memo: A park is an open space where you can play, run, and enjoy nature. Many parks have swings and trees.

questions.question: What is a library for?
questions.ruby_prompt: Libraries are special places. What are they for?
questions.expected: Reading and borrowing books
questions.memo: A library is full of books you can read quietly or take home. Libraries are usually free to use.

questions.question: What can you do at a sports field?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sports fields are open spaces. What do people do there?
options: Play sports like soccer or netball
questions.expected: Play sports like soccer or netball
questions.memo: Sports fields are open spaces for playing sports together. Many South African children play soccer or netball at school.

questions.question: A clinic is a place where you go when you are sick.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? A clinic is a place where you go when you are sick.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — clinics have nurses and sometimes doctors who can check you when you're sick and give you medicine if you need it.

questions.question: On the way to school you pass: your home, the taxi rank, school. Put them in order.
questions.ruby_prompt: Many children go past several places on the way to school. Put these in the right order.
questions.expected: Your home,The taxi rank,School
questions.memo: You start the day at home, then get to a transport place like a taxi rank, then arrive at school.

questions.question: Which one is a clinic?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which building is a clinic?
questions.context: Picture: a building with a red cross sign, a library, a restaurant, a post office.
options: Building with a red cross sign
questions.expected: Building with a red cross sign
questions.memo: Clinics usually have a red cross or first-aid sign. That helps people find them quickly when they are sick.

questions.question: Where do you go to post a letter?
questions.ruby_prompt: If you want to post a letter, where do you go?
questions.expected: The post office
questions.memo: Post offices accept letters and parcels and send them to other places. They also sell stamps.

questions.question: Why is it good to play sports or be active?
questions.ruby_prompt: Playing sports or running around is good for us. Why?
options: It keeps our body healthy and strong
questions.expected: It keeps our body healthy and strong
questions.memo: Moving our body every day keeps our heart, muscles and bones strong. It also helps us sleep better and feel happy.

questions.question: Tell me about one place near where you live.
questions.ruby_prompt: Every neighbourhood has interesting places. Tell me about one near where you live.
questions.expected: There is a park near my house where I play
questions.memo: Any place counts — a park, shop, school, friend's house. Knowing your area helps you feel at home.

questions.question: Where do you go to learn?
questions.ruby_prompt: Where do children go to learn reading, writing and maths?
questions.expected: School
questions.memo: School is where children learn many things together with teachers and friends.

questions.question: What is a market?
questions.ruby_prompt: We hear about markets a lot. What is a market?
options: A place where many people sell food and goods
questions.expected: A place where many people sell food and goods
questions.memo: Markets are busy places where many sellers gather to sell fresh food, clothes and other things. They are an important part of many SA towns.

questions.question: Why is it good to keep fit?
questions.ruby_prompt: Keeping fit is important. Why?
options: It helps your body stay healthy
questions.expected: It helps your body stay healthy
questions.memo: Keeping fit means being active most days — walking, running, playing. A healthy body helps you learn and feel good.

questions.question: Which one is a petrol station?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one is a petrol station?
questions.context: Picture: a place where cars fill up with fuel, a library, a school, a post office.
options: A place where cars fill up with fuel
questions.expected: A place where cars fill up with fuel
questions.memo: Petrol stations sell fuel for cars and taxis. You can also buy some snacks and drinks there.

questions.question: Sleeping all day every day is the best way to keep fit.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Sleeping all day every day is the best way to keep fit.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Sleep is important for rest, but to be fit you also need to move every day — walk, run, play, or do sports.

LS.L1.BKH.T10.title: Family life: now and then
LS.L1.BKH.T10.description: Older family members' experiences, objects from the past, lifestyle then vs now.
LS.L1.BKH.T10.recovery_strategy: Encourage learners to ask their grandparents or older family members one question about 'long ago'. Real family stories make the past come alive.

questions.question: Long ago, how did most people travel?
questions.ruby_prompt: Before there were many cars, how did most people travel?
options: By walking or with animals like horses or oxen
questions.expected: By walking or with animals like horses or oxen
questions.memo: Long ago there were no cars or taxis. People walked, or used horses, donkeys or ox-wagons to travel.

questions.question: Which is something from long ago?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one is something from long ago?
questions.context: Picture: a clay pot, a smartphone, a laptop, a flat-screen TV.
questions.expected: A clay pot
questions.memo: Clay pots have been used for a very long time to cook and store food. Smartphones, laptops and TVs are modern things.

questions.question: What did people use to send messages before there were cellphones?
questions.ruby_prompt: Long ago, there were no cellphones. How did people send messages to family far away?
questions.expected: Paper letters in the post
questions.memo: People wrote letters by hand and sent them through the post office. Letters could take days or weeks to arrive.

questions.question: Who in your family can tell you about life long ago?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some people know stories about long ago. Who in your family can tell you?
questions.expected: Grandparents and older family members
questions.memo: Grandparents and elders have lived a long time. They have stories about what life was like when they were young.

questions.question: Put these ways of travelling in order, from oldest to newest.
questions.ruby_prompt: People have invented new ways to travel over time. Put these in order from oldest to newest.
questions.expected: Walking,Riding a bicycle,Driving a car,Flying in an aeroplane
questions.memo: Humans walked first. Then we invented bicycles, then cars, and finally aeroplanes — each one newer than the last.

questions.question: Tell me one thing your grandparents did differently from you.
questions.ruby_prompt: Life was different long ago. Tell me one thing your grandparents did differently from you.
questions.expected: They walked a long way to school instead of taking a taxi
questions.memo: Any answer works — perhaps they walked far to school, fetched water from a well, listened to the radio instead of TV, or wore different clothes.

questions.question: Children long ago played video games on phones.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Children long ago played video games on phones.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Long ago there were no phones or video games. Children played outside, made their own toys, and played group games.

questions.question: Why is it useful to look at old family photographs?
questions.ruby_prompt: Old family photos show us a lot. Why are they useful?
options: They show us what our family looked like long ago
They are only for throwing away
questions.expected: They show us what our family looked like long ago
questions.memo: Old photos tell stories of our family — where they lived, what they wore, who they loved. They keep memories safe.

questions.question: How did families often get their food long ago?
questions.ruby_prompt: Food today comes from many places. How did most families get food long ago?
options: They grew it, kept animals, or bought from a small local shop
questions.expected: They grew it, kept animals, or bought from a small local shop
questions.memo: Many families had vegetable gardens, kept chickens, or bought from the village shop. Big shops and fast food came much later.

questions.question: Which is an old photograph?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one is an old photograph?
questions.context: Picture: a black-and-white photo, a colour video on a phone, a drawing, a painting.
options: A colour video on a phone
questions.expected: A black-and-white photo
questions.memo: Old photographs were often black-and-white because colour photos were not common long ago. They look different from today's pictures.

questions.question: Why must we keep our bodies fit and healthy?
questions.ruby_prompt: Whether long ago or today, keeping fit is important. Why?
questions.expected: To stay healthy and strong
questions.memo: Healthy bodies let us play, learn and live a long life. Long ago people walked a lot — today we have to remember to move our bodies.

questions.question: How did people wash clothes long ago?
questions.ruby_prompt: Before washing machines, how did people wash their clothes?
options: By hand, in a basin or at the river
questions.expected: By hand, in a basin or at the river
questions.memo: Long ago people washed clothes by hand using a basin or river water and a piece of soap. It was hard work.

questions.question: Your great-grandparents lived a very long time ago.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Your great-grandparents lived a very long time ago.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Great-grandparents are your grandparents' parents. They were born many years before you and have stories from a very different time.

questions.question: Which is something a grandparent might have used long ago?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one is something a grandparent might have used when they were young?
questions.context: Picture: a treadle sewing machine, a tablet computer, a video game console, a smart watch.
questions.expected: A treadle sewing machine
questions.memo: Treadle sewing machines (worked with your feet) were common long ago for making clothes at home. The others are modern.

questions.question: Name one healthy thing you can do every day to stay fit.
questions.ruby_prompt: There are simple things we can do every day to stay fit. Name one.
questions.expected: Walk every day
questions.memo: Walking, running, dancing, playing sports, doing chores — anything that moves your body counts.

LS.L1.BKH.T11.title: Being a good friend
LS.L1.BKH.T11.description: Qualities of a good friend, bullying, recognising and reporting abuse (verbal/physical/sexual). SENSITIVE — scenario-based authoring, not standard recall.
LS.L1.BKH.T11.recovery_strategy: This topic is sensitive. Go slowly. Reassure the learner that all feelings are okay and that telling a trusted grown-up about hurt is always the right thing — never their fault. If a learner struggles, return to gentle role-play with safe scenarios first.

questions.question: Which is a quality of a good friend?
questions.ruby_prompt: Good friends share special qualities. Which one is a quality of a good friend?
options: Kindness and listening when you talk
questions.expected: Kindness and listening when you talk
questions.memo: Good friends listen to each other, are kind, and care about how the other one feels.

questions.question: Your friend is crying because someone hurt their feelings. What is a kind thing to do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Your friend is crying because someone said something hurtful. What is a kind thing to do?
options: Ask them what's wrong and listen
questions.expected: Ask them what's wrong and listen
questions.memo: When a friend is sad, just being there and listening helps a lot. You don't have to fix it — being kind is enough.

questions.question: Which picture shows good friendship?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one shows good friendship?
questions.context: Picture: two children sharing a sandwich, one child taking another's toy, one child pushing another, one child laughing at another alone.
questions.expected: Two children sharing a sandwich
questions.memo: Sharing is a sign of friendship. Taking, pushing, or laughing at someone is not friendly behaviour.

questions.question: What is bullying?
questions.ruby_prompt: We hear the word 'bullying' a lot. What is bullying?
options: Being mean to someone over and over
questions.expected: Being mean to someone over and over
questions.memo: Bullying is when someone is mean to another person on purpose, again and again. It is never okay.

questions.question: If you see someone being bullied at school, what should you do?
questions.ruby_prompt: You see another child being bullied at school. What should you do?
options: Tell a teacher or trusted grown-up
Do nothing and walk away forever
questions.expected: Tell a teacher or trusted grown-up
questions.memo: Telling a teacher or other trusted grown-up is the right thing — it isn't telling tales, it's helping someone who is being hurt.

questions.question: Someone keeps calling you mean names every day. What should you do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Someone is calling you mean names every day at school. What should you do?
options: Tell a parent or teacher you trust
Keep it a secret and feel sad alone
questions.expected: Tell a parent or teacher you trust
questions.memo: You don't have to put up with being hurt. Telling a trusted grown-up means they can help stop it. It is not your fault.

questions.question: What does it mean to be a good friend?
questions.ruby_prompt: In your own words, what does it mean to be a good friend?
questions.expected: To be kind, to listen, and to help when my friend needs me
questions.memo: Good friends are kind, honest, share, listen, and stand up for each other. There are many right answers.

questions.question: A friend asks you to keep a secret that is hurting them. What should you do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Your friend tells you something serious and says 'don't tell anyone'. But it is really hurting them. What should you do?
options: Tell a trusted grown-up — helping is more important than the secret
questions.expected: Tell a trusted grown-up — helping is more important than the secret
questions.memo: Some secrets are not safe to keep. When a friend is being hurt, a trusted grown-up needs to know so they can help. You are being a good friend by telling.

questions.question: If someone touches you in a way that feels wrong or scary, what should you do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sometimes a touch feels wrong or scary. If that happens, what should you do?
options: Tell a parent, teacher, or another trusted grown-up
questions.expected: Tell a parent, teacher, or another trusted grown-up
questions.memo: Your body belongs to you. If a touch feels wrong, it is not your fault — and telling a trusted grown-up is always the right thing to do. They will believe you and help.

questions.question: What can you do if your friend is feeling sad?
questions.ruby_prompt: Your friend looks sad. What is a good thing you can do?
options: Sit with them and ask if they want to talk
questions.expected: Sit with them and ask if they want to talk
questions.memo: Being near a friend when they are sad shows you care. They might want to talk, or just want company.

questions.question: Friends sometimes have arguments. What is the best way to fix it?
questions.ruby_prompt: Even good friends argue sometimes. What is the best way to fix it?
options: Talk about it calmly when you are both ready
questions.expected: Talk about it calmly when you are both ready
questions.memo: Talking calmly helps both friends understand each other. Sometimes saying sorry is part of fixing it.

questions.question: Which picture shows a child being bullied?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one shows a child being bullied?
questions.context: Picture: a child surrounded by laughing children pointing at them, a child playing happily, a child reading a book, a child eating lunch alone but relaxed.
options: A child surrounded by laughing children pointing at them
A child eating lunch alone but relaxed
questions.expected: A child surrounded by laughing children pointing at them
questions.memo: Bullying often looks like people ganging up and laughing at one person. If you see this, tell a teacher.

questions.question: If someone is hurting you with their words or hands, who can you tell?
questions.ruby_prompt: If someone is hurting you with words or hands, who is a safe person to tell?
questions.expected: A parent, a teacher, or another grown-up I trust
questions.memo: You can tell a parent, teacher, school nurse, or any trusted grown-up. They will believe you and help. Some children also call ChildLine on 116 — that is free.

questions.question: Why is it important to tell a grown-up if you are hurt or scared?
questions.ruby_prompt: If you are hurt or scared, why is it important to tell a grown-up?
options: Grown-ups can help and keep you safe
Because you must always be alone
questions.expected: Grown-ups can help and keep you safe
questions.memo: Trusted grown-ups have the power to make things safer. You don't have to handle hard things alone — that is what grown-ups are for.

questions.question: What is one thing a good friend never does on purpose?
questions.ruby_prompt: Good friends do many things. What is one thing a good friend never does on purpose?
questions.expected: Hurt you on purpose
questions.memo: Good friends might make mistakes, but they don't try to hurt you. If someone hurts you on purpose, that's not friendship.

LS.L1.BKH.T12.title: Stories of different South African communities
LS.L1.BKH.T12.description: Stories from diverse SA communities, similarities and differences, customs, festivals, healthy foods.
LS.L1.BKH.T12.recovery_strategy: Celebrate the learner's own culture first, then bridge to others. Use real SA examples — Heritage Day, festivals from different traditions, languages they may hear at home or school.

questions.question: South Africa has many different what?
questions.ruby_prompt: South Africa is a special country because it has many different what?
questions.expected: Cultures and languages
questions.memo: South Africa is known for having many cultures and languages living together. This is why some people call it the Rainbow Nation.

questions.question: What is a 'custom'?
questions.ruby_prompt: We talk about customs in different cultures. What is a custom?
options: A way of doing things in a community
questions.expected: A way of doing things in a community
questions.memo: Customs are special ways a community celebrates, greets, eats or worships. They are often passed from grandparents to parents to children.

questions.question: Which picture shows a festival?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one shows a festival?
questions.context: Picture: people in colourful traditional clothes dancing together, an empty house, a closed shop, a wet road.
options: People in colourful clothes dancing together
questions.expected: People in colourful clothes dancing together
questions.memo: Festivals are celebrations with music, dance, special clothes and food. Different communities have their own festivals.

questions.question: Which is a South African language?
questions.ruby_prompt: South Africa has many languages. Which one is a South African language?
questions.expected: isiZulu
questions.memo: isiZulu is one of South Africa's 11 official languages. Others include English, Afrikaans, isiXhosa, Sesotho, Setswana and more.

questions.question: Why is it good to learn about other cultures?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is it good to learn about cultures that are different from yours?
options: It helps us understand and respect each other
So we can make fun of people
questions.expected: It helps us understand and respect each other
questions.memo: Learning about other people's stories, foods and traditions helps us be kind and respectful. We all live together in South Africa.

questions.question: Which word is a greeting in isiZulu?
questions.ruby_prompt: Different SA languages have different ways to say hello. Which one is a greeting in isiZulu?
questions.expected: Sawubona
questions.memo: 'Sawubona' means 'I see you' in isiZulu. In Sesotho you say 'Dumela', in isiXhosa 'Molo'.

questions.question: Different families can celebrate different special days.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Different families can celebrate different special days.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Some families celebrate Christmas, others Eid, others Diwali, others Heritage Day or family birthdays. All celebrations are special.

questions.question: What can we learn from people from a different culture?
questions.ruby_prompt: Different cultures have lots to share. What can we learn from them?
options: New foods, games, stories and songs
questions.expected: New foods, games, stories and songs
questions.memo: Cultures share food, dance, songs, stories and ways of seeing the world. Learning makes us richer.

questions.question: Lerato's friend celebrates a holiday Lerato has never heard of. What is the kindest thing for Lerato to do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerato's friend Aisha is celebrating a holiday Lerato doesn't know. What is the kindest thing Lerato can do?
options: Ask politely to learn about it
Tell her friend it is wrong
questions.expected: Ask politely to learn about it
questions.memo: Asking politely shows respect and curiosity. It is a kind way to learn about a new tradition.

questions.question: Which is a traditional South African dish?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one is a traditional South African dish?
questions.context: Picture: pap and stew with morogo, a pizza, a hamburger, a doughnut.
questions.expected: Pap and stew with morogo
questions.memo: Pap with stew and morogo (wild spinach) is a traditional, healthy South African meal. The others come from other places.

questions.question: Why do different communities celebrate different festivals?
questions.ruby_prompt: Different communities have different festivals. Why?
options: Because they have different histories and beliefs
questions.expected: Because they have different histories and beliefs
questions.memo: Each community has its own story, beliefs and traditions, so they celebrate different things in their own ways.

questions.question: Tell me one festival or celebration your family enjoys.
questions.ruby_prompt: Every family has special days. Tell me one festival or celebration your family enjoys.
questions.expected: Heritage Day with family braai and traditional clothes
questions.memo: Any answer is welcome — Christmas, Eid, Diwali, Heritage Day, birthdays, family weddings, ancestor ceremonies — all are valid celebrations.

questions.question: Which dish is both traditional and healthy?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some traditional foods are also very healthy. Which is one of them?
questions.expected: Morogo (wild spinach) with pap
questions.memo: Morogo is a wild green vegetable full of goodness. Eaten with pap, it is a healthy traditional meal.

questions.question: How many official languages does South Africa have?
questions.ruby_prompt: South Africa has many languages it officially uses. How many?
questions.memo: South Africa has 11 official languages, which is one of the highest in the world. It shows how many cultures live together here.

questions.question: What is the same about all South Africans, no matter their culture?
questions.ruby_prompt: Even though our cultures are different, what is the same about all South Africans?
options: We are all people who deserve respect
We all eat the same food
We all speak the same language
We all live in the same city
questions.expected: We are all people who deserve respect
questions.memo: South Africans come from many places and traditions, but every single person deserves kindness and respect.

LS.L2.BKH.T01.title: Homes in different places
LS.L2.BKH.T01.description: Types of homes, homes for different weather, mobile homes, safety at home.
LS.L2.BKH.T01.recovery_strategy: If the learner is stuck, start with the home they know best — their own. Then bridge to homes in other places (cities, farms, other countries). Use simple comparisons.

questions.question: Which one is a home?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one is a home where people live?
questions.context: Picture: a house, a hospital, a shop, an office.
questions.expected: A house
questions.memo: A house is a home — a place where people live, sleep and eat together. The others are places to work, shop or get help.

questions.question: What kind of home is best in a very cold, snowy place?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some places are very cold and snowy. What kind of home is best there?
options: An open hut with no walls
questions.expected: A warm, well-insulated house
questions.memo: In cold places, homes need to keep heat inside. That means thick walls, a strong roof, and small windows that close tightly.

questions.question: Long ago, what were many South African homes made from?
questions.ruby_prompt: Houses long ago were not always made of bricks. What were many South African homes made from?
questions.expected: Mud, grass and wood
questions.memo: Many traditional homes were built from local materials — mud, grass and wood. These homes kept families cool in summer and warm in winter.

questions.question: What is a 'mobile home'?
questions.ruby_prompt: We sometimes hear about mobile homes. What is a mobile home?
options: A home that can be moved from one place to another
A home only used by one family
questions.expected: A home that can be moved from one place to another
questions.memo: Mobile homes are built so they can be moved — like a caravan you can pull behind a car. Some families travel and live in them.

questions.question: Which is a safety rule at home?
questions.ruby_prompt: Homes need rules to keep us safe. Which one is a safety rule at home?
options: Do not play with matches or stoves
questions.expected: Do not play with matches or stoves
questions.memo: Matches and stoves can start fires or burn you. Safety rules protect everyone in the home.

questions.question: Why do homes in hot places often have big windows?
questions.ruby_prompt: Houses in hot places often have big windows. Why?
options: To let cool air in and keep the house comfortable
To let in more sun and heat
questions.expected: To let cool air in and keep the house comfortable
questions.memo: Big windows let air flow through the home, which cools it down in hot weather. Homes are designed for the weather around them.

questions.question: Which one is a home in the countryside?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one is a home you would find in the countryside?
questions.context: Picture: a small farm house with fields around, a tall city block of flats, a busy shopping centre, an office tower.
options: A small farm house with fields around
A tall city block of flats
questions.expected: A small farm house with fields around
questions.memo: Homes in the countryside often have land around them. City homes are closer together to fit more people in a smaller space.

questions.question: Different homes look different around the world.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Different homes look different around the world.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — homes look different because the weather, materials, and culture in each place are different. All of them can be lovely homes.

questions.question: Put these home-building steps in the right order.
questions.ruby_prompt: Building a home takes several steps. Put them in the right order.
questions.expected: Choose a piece of land,Lay the foundation,Build the walls,Add the roof
questions.memo: First find the land, then make a strong base (foundation), then build walls, then add the roof to keep rain out. Each step must come in order.

questions.question: Why is it important to know your home address?
questions.ruby_prompt: Knowing where you live is useful. Why is it important to know your home address?
options: So a trusted grown-up can find you or send help
questions.expected: So a trusted grown-up can find you or send help
questions.memo: Knowing your address means people can help you get home, or send help to you if you need it.

questions.question: Tell me one thing you like about your own home.
questions.ruby_prompt: Every home is special. Tell me one thing you like about your own home.
questions.expected: I like that my family is there
questions.memo: Anything counts — the people, a bedroom, the kitchen smells, the garden, the safety. Home is a personal place.

questions.question: Which thing in the kitchen should you never touch when no grown-up is there?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which is dangerous to touch when no grown-up is around?
questions.context: Picture: a hot stove, a wooden spoon, a bowl, a tea towel.
questions.expected: A hot stove
questions.memo: A hot stove can burn you very badly. Only grown-ups should use the stove — even when it looks off, it can still be hot.

questions.question: Why are homes built to suit the weather where they are?
questions.ruby_prompt: Builders think about the weather. Why?
options: So the people inside are comfortable in any season
questions.expected: So the people inside are comfortable in any season
questions.memo: Hot places need cool homes, cold places need warm homes, rainy places need strong roofs. The weather shapes the home.

questions.question: If you smell smoke and see fire at home, what should you do first?
questions.ruby_prompt: You smell smoke and see fire at home. What is the very first thing to do?
options: Get out and call a grown-up loudly
Try to put it out alone
questions.expected: Get out and call a grown-up loudly
questions.memo: Getting out and getting a grown-up keeps you safe. Hiding makes it hard to find you, and small children should not try to fight fires.

questions.question: Name one type of home you have seen or heard about.
questions.ruby_prompt: Homes come in many shapes. Name one type of home you have seen or heard about.
questions.expected: A flat in a block of flats
questions.memo: Houses, flats, RDP houses, farmhouses, huts, caravans — any home counts. Different homes suit different families.

LS.L2.BKH.T02.title: Water
LS.L2.BKH.T02.description: Sources, purification, water cycle, aquatic life, water safety, effects of dirty water.
LS.L2.BKH.T02.recovery_strategy: If a learner is stuck on the water cycle, draw it with them — sun, sea, clouds, rain, river, sea again. Hands-on or visual works better than words alone.

questions.question: Which is a safe source of drinking water?
questions.ruby_prompt: Not all water is safe to drink. Which one is a safe source?
options: A tap with clean municipal water
questions.expected: A tap with clean municipal water
questions.memo: Tap water is cleaned at a water plant so it is safe to drink. Puddles, rivers and stagnant water can carry germs.

questions.question: What can you do to make unsafe water safer?
questions.ruby_prompt: If water might not be clean, what can a family do to make it safer?
options: Leave it in the sun for an hour
questions.expected: Boil it before drinking
questions.memo: Boiling water for a few minutes kills most germs. It is a common way to make water safer when there's no clean tap.

questions.question: Put these water-cycle steps in order.
questions.ruby_prompt: Water moves around our planet in a cycle. Put the steps in order.
options: Sun heats water in the sea
Water rises into the sky as vapour
Rain flows in rivers back to the sea
questions.expected: Sun heats water in the sea,Water rises into the sky as vapour,Clouds form and it rains,Rain flows in rivers back to the sea
questions.memo: The sun warms water and turns it into vapour. The vapour rises, cools, and forms clouds. Then it rains, and water flows back to the sea.

questions.question: Which animal lives in water?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which animal lives in water?
