questions.context: Picture: a fish, a chicken, a cat, an ant.
questions.expected: A fish
questions.memo: Fish live in water and breathe through gills. Chickens, cats and ants live on land.

questions.question: What can happen if you drink dirty water?
questions.ruby_prompt: Dirty water can hurt people. What can happen if you drink it?
options: You can get sick with a sore tummy or diarrhoea
questions.expected: You can get sick with a sore tummy or diarrhoea
questions.memo: Dirty water can carry germs that make people very sick. That is why we always drink clean water.

questions.question: Why must children never swim alone?
questions.ruby_prompt: Children should not swim alone. Why?
options: Water can be deeper or stronger than it looks, and a grown-up can help if there is trouble
questions.expected: Water can be deeper or stronger than it looks, and a grown-up can help if there is trouble
questions.memo: Even shallow water can be dangerous. A grown-up nearby can help if you slip or get tired. Always swim with someone responsible.

questions.question: Water from a clean tap is always safe to drink.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Water from a clean tap is always safe to drink.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: In South Africa, water from a clean municipal tap has been treated and is generally safe to drink. If the tap is broken or the water looks strange, ask a grown-up.

questions.question: Where can water come from in nature?
questions.ruby_prompt: Water in nature comes from many places. Which one is a natural water source?
questions.expected: Rivers, dams and rain
questions.memo: Water in nature comes from rivers, dams, lakes, rain and underground springs. People collect and clean it for us to use.

questions.question: Which is a water safety rule near a swimming pool?
questions.ruby_prompt: Swimming pools can be fun and dangerous. Which one is a safety rule?
options: Never run on the wet pool edge
questions.expected: Never run on the wet pool edge
questions.memo: Wet pool edges are slippery and you can fall and hurt yourself. Walking, not running, keeps everyone safe.

questions.question: Name one way you can save water at home.
questions.ruby_prompt: South Africa often has water shortages. Name one way you can save water at home.
questions.expected: Close the tap while brushing my teeth
questions.memo: Saving water means turning off taps when not in use, taking shorter showers, fixing leaks, and reusing water for plants.

questions.question: What makes clouds in the sky?
questions.ruby_prompt: Clouds float high in the sky. What are they made of?
options: Tiny drops of water and ice
questions.expected: Tiny drops of water and ice
questions.memo: Clouds are tiny droplets of water and ice high in the air. When they get heavy enough, they release rain.

questions.question: Which one is a creature that lives in the sea?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which creature lives in the sea?
questions.context: Picture: a dolphin, a cow, a chicken, a sheep.
questions.expected: A dolphin
questions.memo: Dolphins live in the sea. The other three are land animals you find on farms.

questions.question: Why must we not waste water?
questions.ruby_prompt: Saving water matters. Why must we not waste it?
options: Clean water is precious and there is not always enough
questions.expected: Clean water is precious and there is not always enough
questions.memo: Many places in South Africa do not have enough water. Saving it means there is enough for drinking, washing and cooking for everyone.

questions.question: Sipho sees his friend slip and fall into a deep pool. What should Sipho do first?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho's friend has fallen into a deep pool. What should Sipho do first?
questions.expected: Shout for a grown-up loudly
questions.memo: Children should not jump in to rescue someone — they can drown too. Shouting for a grown-up gets the right help fast.

questions.question: Rain comes from the clouds.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Rain comes from the clouds.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: When the tiny water droplets in a cloud join together and get heavy, they fall as rain. That is part of the water cycle.

LS.L2.BKH.T03.title: Weather and seasons
LS.L2.BKH.T03.description: Weather observation, seasonal changes, suitable clothing, effects on plants/animals/fruit.
LS.L2.BKH.T03.recovery_strategy: Help the learner notice the weather each morning for a week. Real observation builds vocabulary faster than worksheets.

questions.question: What kind of clothes do you wear on a very hot day?
questions.ruby_prompt: On a very hot day, what kind of clothes are best?
options: Light, cool clothes and a sun hat
questions.expected: Light, cool clothes and a sun hat
questions.memo: Light clothes let air through and keep you cool. A sun hat protects your face and head from the sun.

questions.question: Which season is the coldest in South Africa?
questions.ruby_prompt: South Africa has four seasons. Which one is the coldest?
questions.expected: Winter
questions.memo: Winter (June, July, August) is the coldest season in South Africa. In some places it even snows.

questions.question: Put these seasons in order, starting from summer.
questions.ruby_prompt: Seasons happen in a regular order. Drag them starting from summer.
questions.expected: Summer,Autumn,Winter,Spring
questions.memo: After summer, leaves fall in autumn. Then winter is cold. Then spring brings new leaves, and summer comes back again.

questions.question: Which fruit is most often ready to eat in summer in South Africa?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some fruits ripen in summer. Which one is most often a summer fruit in SA?
questions.expected: Mangoes and peaches
questions.memo: Mangoes and peaches ripen in the warm South African summer. Different fruits come in different seasons.

questions.question: What protects you best from the sun on a hot day?
questions.ruby_prompt: On a sunny day, what protects you best?
options: A hat, sunscreen, and staying in the shade
questions.expected: A hat, sunscreen, and staying in the shade
questions.memo: Sun can burn skin and hurt eyes. A hat shades your face, sunscreen protects your skin, and shade keeps you cooler.

questions.question: What happens to many trees in autumn?
questions.ruby_prompt: Many trees change in autumn. What happens?
options: Their leaves turn yellow or brown and fall down
questions.expected: Their leaves turn yellow or brown and fall down
questions.memo: In autumn, many trees lose their leaves. The colours change first, then the leaves drop. New leaves grow back in spring.

questions.question: Which one is a winter scene?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one is a winter scene?
questions.context: Picture: bare trees with frost, a sunny beach, a green garden with flowers, a hot summer braai.
options: A green garden full of flowers
questions.expected: Bare trees with frost
questions.memo: Winter often shows bare trees and frost or snow. The other pictures are signs of warmer seasons.

questions.question: What is a 'weather chart'?
questions.ruby_prompt: We use weather charts at school. What is a weather chart?
options: A record of the weather over several days
questions.expected: A record of the weather over several days
questions.memo: A weather chart helps us see patterns — like how often it rains in a week, or which day is hottest. Scientists use them to study climate.

questions.question: Spring brings new what?
questions.ruby_prompt: After winter comes spring. Spring brings new what?
questions.expected: Leaves and flowers
questions.memo: Spring is when plants wake up. New green leaves and bright flowers appear, and the weather warms up.

questions.question: Why is it good to drink more water on a hot day?
questions.ruby_prompt: On a very hot day, why is it good to drink more water?
options: Your body loses water through sweating
questions.expected: Your body loses water through sweating
questions.memo: When you sweat to stay cool, your body loses water. Drinking more water keeps you healthy and stops you feeling dizzy.

questions.question: Tell me one thing you like about your favourite season.
questions.ruby_prompt: Every season has something nice. Tell me one thing you like about your favourite season.
questions.expected: I love summer because we can swim
questions.memo: Any answer works — beach in summer, warm fires in winter, flowers in spring, falling leaves in autumn.

questions.question: It snows everywhere in South Africa in winter.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? It snows everywhere in South Africa in winter.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Snow only falls in a few cold areas of South Africa, like the high parts of the Drakensberg. Many parts of the country are cool but dry in winter.

questions.question: What do many animals do in winter?
questions.ruby_prompt: Animals change with the seasons. What do many animals do in winter?
options: Stay warmer with thicker fur or hide in burrows
Grow new feathers in bright pink
questions.expected: Stay warmer with thicker fur or hide in burrows
questions.memo: Many animals grow thicker fur in winter, or hide in burrows to stay warm. They have their own ways to survive the cold.

questions.question: If a big storm is coming, what should your family do?
questions.ruby_prompt: A big storm is forecast for tonight. What should your family do?
options: Stay safely inside until the storm passes
questions.expected: Stay safely inside until the storm passes
questions.memo: Big storms can have lightning and strong winds. Staying inside keeps you safe. Tall trees and open fields are dangerous in storms.

questions.question: Which season usually has the most rain in many parts of South Africa?
questions.ruby_prompt: Different parts of SA have different rainy seasons. In many parts, which season has the most rain?
questions.expected: Summer
questions.memo: Most of South Africa gets its rain in summer (with afternoon thunderstorms). The Western Cape is different — it gets winter rain.

LS.L2.BKH.T04.title: How my body works
LS.L2.BKH.T04.description: External and internal organs and their functions, skeleton, body care, healthy lifestyle.
LS.L2.BKH.T04.recovery_strategy: Pair every body-part name with a movement the learner can do — squeeze a hand, listen to a heartbeat through the chest. The body teaches itself.

questions.question: What is the job of your heart?
questions.ruby_prompt: Your heart works all day, even when you sleep. What does it do?
options: It pumps blood around your body
It carries you when you walk
questions.expected: It pumps blood around your body
questions.memo: Your heart is a strong muscle in your chest. It pumps blood that carries food and oxygen to every part of your body.

questions.question: What do your lungs do?
questions.ruby_prompt: We breathe in and out all day. What do our lungs do?
options: They take in air and give your body oxygen
questions.expected: They take in air and give your body oxygen
questions.memo: Lungs are like balloons in your chest. When you breathe in, they fill with air so your body can use the oxygen.

questions.question: Which body part helps you see?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which body part helps you see?
questions.context: Picture: an eye, an ear, a hand, a foot.
questions.expected: Eye
questions.memo: Eyes let us see colours, shapes and movement. Without them we would have to use other senses to know the world.

questions.question: What is your skeleton for?
questions.ruby_prompt: Inside your body you have a skeleton. What is it for?
options: It holds your body up and protects your organs
questions.expected: It holds your body up and protects your organs
questions.memo: Your skeleton is the bony frame inside your body. Without it you would not be able to stand up or walk.

questions.question: Which one is something inside your body?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some body parts are on the outside, some are on the inside. Which one is inside?
questions.expected: The liver
questions.memo: The liver is an organ inside your tummy that helps clean your blood. Noses, fingers and hair are on the outside.

questions.question: How can you look after your teeth?
questions.ruby_prompt: Our teeth need looking after. How?
options: Brush twice a day and avoid too many sweets
questions.expected: Brush twice a day and avoid too many sweets
questions.memo: Brushing in the morning and at night keeps your teeth healthy. Less sugar means fewer holes (cavities).

questions.question: Put these steps for staying healthy in any order: eat well, sleep, drink water, exercise.
questions.ruby_prompt: Healthy habits go together. Choose any sensible order to do them in a day.
questions.expected: Eat a healthy breakfast,Drink water during the day,Exercise or play actively,Sleep enough at night
questions.memo: A healthy day usually starts with breakfast, includes water and play, and ends with a good night's sleep. Doing all of these keeps your body strong.

questions.question: Your body is made of many parts that work together.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Your body is made of many parts that work together.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — bones, muscles, blood, organs and skin all work together to keep you alive. Each part has a job.

questions.question: What helps your bones grow strong?
questions.ruby_prompt: Healthy food helps your bones grow strong. Which food is especially good for bones?
options: Milk, cheese and leafy green vegetables
questions.expected: Milk, cheese and leafy green vegetables
questions.memo: Calcium helps build strong bones. You get it from milk, cheese, yoghurt and leafy greens like morogo.

questions.question: What sense do you use to taste food?
questions.ruby_prompt: Eating tastes good because of one of your senses. Which one?
questions.expected: Taste, using your tongue
questions.memo: Your tongue has tiny taste buds that pick up sweet, salty, sour and bitter. Smell helps too — that's why food tastes different when you have a blocked nose.

questions.question: Tell me one thing you can do to look after your body.
questions.ruby_prompt: Looking after your body is a daily job. Tell me one thing you can do.
questions.expected: Wash my hands before eating
questions.memo: Anything caring counts — eating well, sleeping enough, washing, exercising, wearing seatbelts, brushing teeth.

questions.question: Which body part helps you balance?
questions.ruby_prompt: When you walk on a beam or stand on one foot, which body parts help?
options: Your ears and your eyes work together
questions.expected: Your ears and your eyes work together
questions.memo: Your inner ear and your eyes both help you stay balanced. That is why you sometimes wobble when you spin around — your ears get confused.

questions.question: Why is sleep important?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sleep is just as important as food. Why?
options: Your body and brain rest and grow when you sleep
Sleep is a waste of time
questions.expected: Your body and brain rest and grow when you sleep
questions.memo: When you sleep your body fixes itself, grows, and stores what you learned during the day. Children need a lot of sleep.

questions.question: What does your tongue do besides tasting?
questions.ruby_prompt: Your tongue tastes food, but it does another important job. What?
options: It carries food across the floor
questions.expected: It helps you speak
questions.memo: Your tongue moves to make the sounds of words. Without it, talking would be very hard.

questions.question: Which body part should you protect when riding a bicycle?
questions.ruby_prompt: When you ride a bike, one body part especially needs protection. Which one?
options: Your head — by wearing a helmet
questions.expected: Your head — by wearing a helmet
questions.memo: Your brain is in your head, and a head injury can be very serious. A helmet protects your head if you fall off.

LS.L2.BKH.T05.title: Foods eaten by different communities
LS.L2.BKH.T05.description: Dietary choices across communities, world foods, cooking methods, recipes, food allergies.
LS.L2.BKH.T05.recovery_strategy: Connect to foods the learner already eats. Compare with one or two cultures they might know. Don't push too many examples at once.

questions.question: Which food is eaten in many South African homes?
questions.ruby_prompt: South African families eat many lovely foods. Which one is eaten in many homes here?
questions.expected: Pap and stew
questions.memo: Pap (maize porridge) with stew is eaten across many South African families. Other foods are popular too, but pap is widely loved.

questions.question: Which food comes from Italy?
questions.ruby_prompt: Different countries have different favourite foods. Which one is from Italy?
questions.expected: Pasta and pizza
questions.memo: Pasta and pizza are well-known Italian foods. Today people all over the world enjoy them.

questions.question: Where might 'bunny chow' have come from?
questions.ruby_prompt: Bunny chow is a famous South African food. Where in SA did it come from?
questions.expected: Durban — the Indian community there
questions.memo: Bunny chow is a hollowed-out bread filled with curry, started by the Indian community in Durban. It is now loved all over SA.

questions.question: Which one is a food many people are allergic to?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some foods can make people very sick if they are allergic. Which is a common one?
questions.expected: Peanuts
questions.memo: Some people are very allergic to peanuts and can get very sick. That's why we ask before sharing food and never force a friend to eat something.

questions.question: Put these baking-bread steps in order.
questions.ruby_prompt: Baking bread takes several steps. Put them in order.
options: Add yeast and let the dough rise
questions.expected: Mix flour and water,Add yeast and let the dough rise,Bake in the oven,Eat it warm
questions.memo: Bread starts as flour and water. Yeast makes the dough rise. The oven bakes it golden, and then we get to eat it.

questions.question: What is a 'recipe'?
questions.ruby_prompt: Cooks use recipes to make food. What is a recipe?
options: A list of ingredients and steps to make a dish
questions.expected: A list of ingredients and steps to make a dish
questions.memo: A recipe is the instructions for making something. It tells you what to use and what to do.

questions.question: Different families and cultures eat different foods.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Different families and cultures eat different foods.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — every culture has favourite foods. They are all valid. Trying new foods is a way to learn about other cultures.

questions.question: What should you do if a friend tells you they cannot eat something because of an allergy?
questions.ruby_prompt: Your friend Aisha says she can't eat peanuts because of an allergy. What should you do?
options: Respect it and don't try to share peanut food with her
Try to make her eat one anyway
questions.expected: Respect it and don't try to share peanut food with her
questions.memo: Food allergies are serious — eating the wrong thing can make someone really sick. Believing your friend and respecting it is kind and safe.

questions.question: Which one is a vegetarian meal?
questions.ruby_prompt: Vegetarian means no meat. Which one is a vegetarian meal?
questions.expected: Beans, rice and vegetables
questions.memo: A vegetarian meal has no meat or fish. Beans, lentils and vegetables give the body lots of goodness without meat.

questions.question: Tell me about a meal your family loves.
questions.ruby_prompt: Every family has favourite meals. Tell me about one your family loves.
questions.expected: My family loves to braai chicken on Sunday
questions.memo: Family meals are special. Sharing yours helps others learn about your home and culture.

questions.question: Which one is a dish from India that many South Africans enjoy?
questions.ruby_prompt: Indian food is part of SA cuisine. Which dish is from India?
questions.expected: Curry and roti
questions.memo: Curry and roti come from Indian cooking and are loved in many South African homes, especially in Durban.

questions.question: Why is it kind to try new foods that friends share?
questions.ruby_prompt: Friends sometimes share food from their culture. Why is it kind to try it?
options: It shows respect and helps you learn about their family
questions.expected: It shows respect and helps you learn about their family
questions.memo: Trying new food is a kind way to show interest in someone's culture. (If you have allergies, of course you check first.)

questions.question: Which food gives you energy to play and learn?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some foods give your body energy. Which one does that?
options: Bread, rice, pap and other grains
questions.expected: Bread, rice, pap and other grains
questions.memo: Grains like bread, rice and pap have carbohydrates, which give your body energy to run, jump and learn.

questions.question: What does it mean if food has 'gone off' or is rotten?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sometimes food goes off. What does that mean?
options: It is no longer safe to eat and could make you sick
It just tastes a little different
questions.expected: It is no longer safe to eat and could make you sick
questions.memo: Food that smells bad, looks slimy or has mould has gone off. Eating it can give you food poisoning, so throw it away.

questions.question: Name one food that is eaten in your home and tell me why your family likes it.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me a food your family eats and why they love it.
questions.expected: We eat samp and beans because my grandmother taught us
questions.memo: Family foods carry love and tradition. Whatever you share is the right answer.

LS.L2.BKH.T06.title: Energy resources
LS.L2.BKH.T06.description: Types of energy (electricity, petrol, paraffin, solar, wind, wood), home/school usage, hazards, first aid.
LS.L2.BKH.T06.recovery_strategy: Tie energy talk to things the learner can see — the stove, the lights, the kettle, a car. Energy is invisible, so concrete examples are essential.

questions.question: Which one is a source of energy at home?
questions.ruby_prompt: Homes use different kinds of energy. Which one is a source of energy?
questions.expected: Electricity
questions.memo: Electricity powers our lights, fridges and TVs. It is one of the most common types of energy at home.

questions.question: Where does solar energy come from?
questions.ruby_prompt: Solar panels work by themselves outside. Where does solar energy come from?
questions.expected: The sun
questions.memo: Solar means 'from the sun'. Solar panels catch the sun's energy and turn it into electricity, even on partly cloudy days.

questions.question: What can a fire from a paraffin stove cause?
questions.ruby_prompt: Paraffin stoves help cook, but they can be dangerous. What can they cause if used carelessly?
options: A house fire and serious injuries
questions.expected: A house fire and serious injuries
questions.memo: Paraffin can spill and catch fire easily. Many home fires start this way. Stoves should be on a stable surface, away from curtains and kept away from children.

questions.question: Which one uses electricity at home?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one uses electricity at home?
questions.context: Picture: a fridge, a wooden chair, a candle, a paper book.
questions.expected: A fridge
questions.memo: Fridges need electricity to keep food cold. Chairs, candles and books work without electricity.

questions.question: What should you do if you see frayed or damaged electric wires?
questions.ruby_prompt: You see wires at home that look frayed or damaged. What should you do?
options: Tell a grown-up — never touch them
Pull on them to see what happens
questions.expected: Tell a grown-up — never touch them
questions.memo: Damaged wires can shock you very badly, sometimes deadly. Always tell a grown-up so they can call a qualified electrician.

questions.question: Why should we save electricity at home?
questions.ruby_prompt: South African families try to save electricity. Why?
options: To use less and to help everyone have enough
Because the lights are too bright
questions.expected: To use less and to help everyone have enough
questions.memo: Saving electricity means there is more to go around, your family pays less, and it is better for the planet too.

questions.question: Put these first-aid steps in order for a small burn.
questions.ruby_prompt: If someone has a small burn at home, what steps should be done? Put them in order.
options: Hold the burn under cool running water
Visit a clinic if it is serious
questions.expected: Tell a grown-up,Hold the burn under cool running water,Cover with a clean cloth,Visit a clinic if it is serious
questions.memo: For small burns: tell a grown-up first, then cool it with water for several minutes, then cover lightly. If it blisters or is large, see a nurse.

questions.question: Wind power uses wind to make electricity.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Wind power uses wind to make electricity.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — large wind turbines (looking like giant fans) catch the wind and turn it into electricity. They make energy without polluting.

questions.question: What is one way to save energy at home?
questions.ruby_prompt: Saving energy helps everyone. Name one way to save energy at home.
options: Switch off lights when you leave a room
Leave every light on all night
Open the fridge for a long time
Boil more water than you need
questions.expected: Switch off lights when you leave a room
questions.memo: Small habits save lots of energy — switching off lights, closing the fridge quickly, boiling only the water you need.

questions.question: Which fuel do most cars use?
questions.ruby_prompt: Most cars need fuel to run. Which one do they use?
questions.expected: Petrol or diesel
questions.memo: Cars use petrol or diesel from petrol stations. Today, some new cars use electricity from batteries instead.

questions.question: Which one is safe to do during a thunderstorm?
questions.ruby_prompt: During a thunderstorm, which is the safe thing to do?
options: Stay inside and away from open windows
questions.expected: Stay inside and away from open windows
questions.memo: Lightning is dangerous. Tall trees, open fields, water and metal can all attract it. Stay inside and wait it out.

questions.question: Name one energy source you have heard of.
questions.ruby_prompt: We use many energy sources every day. Name one you have heard of.
questions.expected: Electricity
questions.memo: Electricity, petrol, diesel, paraffin, wood, gas, solar, and wind are all energy sources. Any one counts.

questions.question: Why is it never okay to put your finger in a plug socket?
questions.ruby_prompt: Plug sockets look like little holes — but they are dangerous. Why?
options: Electricity inside can shock and badly hurt you
questions.expected: Electricity inside can shock and badly hurt you
questions.memo: Plug sockets carry strong electricity that can shock, burn, or even kill. Never push anything into a socket.

questions.question: What is a fire extinguisher?
questions.ruby_prompt: You may have seen a red bottle on a wall called a fire extinguisher. What does it do?
options: It is a tool grown-ups use to put out small fires
questions.expected: It is a tool grown-ups use to put out small fires
questions.memo: Fire extinguishers shoot out something that smothers a small fire. Children should call a grown-up first — they know how to use them.

questions.question: Why is the sun a special source of energy?
questions.ruby_prompt: The sun gives the planet energy. Why is the sun special?
options: It is free and does not run out
questions.expected: It is free and does not run out
questions.memo: Solar energy from the sun is renewable — we cannot use it up. Using solar makes less pollution than burning fuels.

LS.L2.BKH.T07.title: Wild animals
LS.L2.BKH.T07.description: Common SA wild animals, classifications (herbivore/carnivore/omnivore), animal diseases.
LS.L2.BKH.T07.recovery_strategy: Tie wild-animal facts to learners' own experience — a visit to a game reserve, an animal seen on TV, a photo book. Real images beat abstract descriptions.

questions.question: Which one is a South African wild animal?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one is a South African wild animal?
questions.context: Picture: a springbok, a chicken, a cat, a sheep.
questions.expected: A springbok
questions.memo: Springboks live wild in South Africa. The others are farm or pet animals that live with people.

questions.question: What does a 'herbivore' eat?
questions.ruby_prompt: Animals that only eat plants are called herbivores. What do herbivores eat?
questions.expected: Plants — grass, leaves and fruit
questions.memo: Herbivores like elephants, zebras and giraffes only eat plants. Their bodies are made for grazing or chewing leaves.

questions.question: What does a 'carnivore' eat?
questions.ruby_prompt: Carnivores have a different diet from herbivores. What do they eat?
questions.expected: Mostly other animals (meat)
questions.memo: Carnivores like lions and cheetahs eat meat. They hunt other animals to survive.

questions.question: Lions are an example of which group?
questions.ruby_prompt: Lions are famous wild animals. Which group of eaters are they?
questions.expected: Carnivores
questions.memo: Lions are top carnivores. They live in groups called prides and hunt large prey together.

questions.question: An elephant is the largest land animal in South Africa.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? An elephant is the largest land animal in South Africa.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — African elephants are the biggest land animals on Earth. You can see them in many South African game reserves like Kruger.

questions.question: Which animal has black-and-white stripes?
questions.ruby_prompt: South Africa is home to a famous striped animal. Which one?
questions.expected: A zebra
questions.memo: Zebras have black and white stripes. The stripes help them confuse predators and tell each other apart.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to feed wild animals at a game park?
questions.ruby_prompt: At game parks signs say 'Do not feed the animals'. Why?
options: Wild animals can become unsafe and lose their natural skills
questions.expected: Wild animals can become unsafe and lose their natural skills
questions.memo: When wild animals get used to people for food, they stop hunting and become dangerous. Keep wild animals wild by leaving them alone.

questions.question: Put these wild animals in order from smallest to largest.
questions.ruby_prompt: Animals come in many sizes. Put them in order from smallest to largest.
questions.expected: Meerkat,Springbok,Zebra,Elephant
questions.memo: Meerkats are small, springboks bigger, zebras heavier, and elephants the biggest of these four.

questions.question: Which animal lives at the very top of South Africa's tall grass — its long neck helps it eat from trees?
questions.ruby_prompt: There is one tall African animal with a very long neck. What is it?
questions.expected: A giraffe
questions.memo: Giraffes are the tallest animals on Earth. Their long necks let them reach leaves high in trees that other animals cannot reach.

questions.question: Tell me one wild animal you have seen or heard about.
questions.ruby_prompt: Wild animals are everywhere in stories and pictures. Tell me one you know.
questions.expected: A lion
questions.memo: Any wild animal counts — lion, leopard, rhino, hippo, springbok, baboon, vulture. They are all part of South Africa's wildlife.

questions.question: Which one is a wild predator?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one is a wild predator?
questions.context: Picture: a leopard, a zebra, an antelope, a rabbit.
questions.expected: A leopard
questions.memo: Leopards are predators — they hunt other animals. Zebras, antelope and rabbits are prey animals that eat plants.

questions.question: Why must wild animals be protected from poachers?
questions.ruby_prompt: Poachers are people who kill wild animals illegally. Why must we protect animals from them?
options: Some species could disappear forever if too many are killed
questions.expected: Some species could disappear forever if too many are killed
questions.memo: When too many animals of one kind are killed, they can go extinct — gone for ever. Rhinos and elephants are in danger from poachers. Protecting them keeps SA's wildlife alive.

questions.question: Which animal lives in water and looks like a giant pig?
questions.ruby_prompt: There's an SA wild animal that spends most of the day in rivers. Which one?
questions.expected: A hippo
questions.memo: Hippos spend most of the day in rivers and lakes to stay cool. They look slow but are fast and very strong.

questions.question: Wild animals can carry diseases that affect other animals or people.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Wild animals can carry diseases that affect other animals or people.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Some wild animals carry diseases like rabies. That's why we never approach wild animals and report any bites to a clinic immediately.

questions.question: Why are game reserves like Kruger important?
questions.ruby_prompt: Game reserves cover huge areas. Why are they important?
options: They give wild animals a safe place to live
questions.expected: They give wild animals a safe place to live
questions.memo: Game reserves protect animals and the land they live on. Without them, many SA species would have disappeared by now.

LS.L2.BKH.T08.title: Relationships and handling emotions
LS.L2.BKH.T08.description: Different relationships, emotions in different situations, handling emotions, classroom behaviour, exercise to manage feelings. SENSITIVE — scenario-based authoring.
LS.L2.BKH.T08.recovery_strategy: This is a sensitive topic. Slow down, use stories and role-play, and never make a learner feel that a feeling is 'wrong'. The lesson is: feelings are okay, hurtful actions are not, and trusted grown-ups help.

questions.question: Which feeling might you have when something nice happens?
questions.ruby_prompt: When something nice happens, what feeling might you have?
questions.expected: Happiness or excitement
questions.memo: Nice events usually bring nice feelings — joy, excitement, calm. Naming feelings helps us understand ourselves.

questions.question: It is okay to feel sad sometimes.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? It is okay to feel sad sometimes.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: All feelings are okay — sad, angry, scared, happy. Feelings come and go. We don't have to be happy all the time.

questions.question: Lerato is angry because her brother broke her toy. What is a healthy thing she can do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerato's brother broke her toy. She is very angry. What is a healthy thing she can do?
options: Tell a grown-up and talk about how she feels
Keep all her anger inside forever
questions.expected: Tell a grown-up and talk about how she feels
questions.memo: Anger is okay to feel. Talking about it helps us calm down. Hurting people or things doesn't fix anything — it makes things worse.

questions.question: What is one way to calm down when you are very angry?
questions.ruby_prompt: When anger feels big inside you, what is one way to calm down?
options: Hold your breath until you faint
questions.expected: Take slow, deep breaths
questions.memo: Slow breathing calms your body. Counting to ten, walking away, or talking to someone can also help. These are healthy ways to handle big feelings.

questions.question: Who is in your immediate family?
questions.ruby_prompt: Your immediate family is the people closest to you. Who is usually in your immediate family?
options: Parents, brothers, sisters or carers who live with you
questions.expected: Parents, brothers, sisters or carers who live with you
questions.memo: Immediate family is the household — the people you live with and who care for you. Other family members (cousins, grandparents) are also family, but a bit further out.

questions.question: Your friend looks worried and won't tell you why. What is the kindest thing to do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Your friend looks worried but doesn't want to say why. What is kind to do?
options: Let them know you are there and a grown-up can also help
questions.expected: Let them know you are there and a grown-up can also help
questions.memo: Sometimes friends aren't ready to talk. Being patient and reminding them grown-ups can help is kind. Forcing or gossiping makes things worse.

questions.question: What can help your body feel better when feelings are heavy?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sometimes feelings make our body heavy. What can help?
options: Exercise like walking, running or playing
Lying still for a whole day
questions.expected: Exercise like walking, running or playing
questions.memo: Moving your body releases the heavy feelings. Even a short walk or play time can change how you feel.

questions.question: If you feel very sad for a long time, what should you do?
questions.ruby_prompt: If sadness stays for many days and won't go away, what should you do?
options: Tell a parent, teacher, or another trusted grown-up
Pretend you are happy when you are not
questions.expected: Tell a parent, teacher, or another trusted grown-up
questions.memo: Sadness that lasts a long time is too heavy to carry alone. A trusted grown-up can listen, hug you, and find more help if you need it. You are never a burden for telling.

questions.question: What is a healthy way to share your feelings?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sharing feelings keeps us healthy. What is a healthy way to do it?
questions.expected: Talk to someone I trust
questions.memo: Talking to a trusted person, writing in a journal, or drawing can all help. There are many right answers — the main thing is not keeping feelings stuck inside.

questions.question: Which relationship is between a teacher and a learner?
questions.ruby_prompt: Different relationships have different roles. What kind of relationship is between a teacher and a learner?
options: A caring relationship where the teacher helps the learner grow
questions.expected: A caring relationship where the teacher helps the learner grow
questions.memo: Teachers care about their learners and help them learn. They are not parents, but they look after you at school.

questions.question: Which picture shows children working well in a group?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one shows good group work?
questions.context: Picture: children listening to each other and sharing materials, one child grabbing all the materials, two children fighting, a child sitting alone refusing to help.
options: Children listening to each other and sharing
One child grabbing all the materials
A child sitting alone refusing to help
questions.expected: Children listening to each other and sharing
questions.memo: Good group work means listening, sharing, and taking turns. Everyone gets a chance to speak and be helpful.

questions.question: Tell me one feeling you sometimes have at school.
questions.ruby_prompt: School brings many feelings. Tell me one feeling you sometimes have.
questions.expected: I feel happy when I see my friends
questions.memo: All feelings at school are okay — excited, nervous, proud, sad, bored. Naming a feeling is the first step to handling it.

questions.question: It is okay to cry when you are sad.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? It is okay to cry when you are sad.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Crying is the body's natural way to let out big feelings. Boys and girls can cry. It is healthy.

questions.question: What is the best response when a friend is mean to you?
questions.ruby_prompt: A friend is mean to you. What is the best thing to do?
options: Calmly tell them it hurt, and tell a grown-up if it keeps happening
Keep quiet and let it keep happening
questions.expected: Calmly tell them it hurt, and tell a grown-up if it keeps happening
questions.memo: Speaking up calmly can help fix things. If the meanness keeps going, a trusted grown-up should know — it is not 'telling tales', it is asking for help.

questions.question: Why is it important to talk about our feelings?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is it important to talk about our feelings instead of holding them in?
options: Feelings get smaller when we share them with a trusted person
questions.expected: Feelings get smaller when we share them with a trusted person
questions.memo: Talking with someone who cares helps feelings feel less heavy. You don't have to handle big feelings alone.

LS.L2.BKH.T09.title: Keeping our environment clean
LS.L2.BKH.T09.description: Healthy home/school/local environment, hygiene-related diseases (diarrhoea, TB).
LS.L2.BKH.T09.recovery_strategy: Use the learner's own school and home as the case study. 'What rubbish do you see on your walk to school?' is more powerful than abstract environment talk.

questions.question: What should you do with a sweet wrapper after eating?
questions.ruby_prompt: You finished a sweet. What should you do with the wrapper?
questions.expected: Put it in a bin
questions.memo: Bins keep our schools and streets clean. Litter on the ground or in rivers hurts the environment and animals.

questions.question: Why must we keep our home clean?
questions.ruby_prompt: Keeping our home clean is important. Why?
options: So we stay healthy and free from germs
Because it looks nice for visitors only
questions.expected: So we stay healthy and free from germs
questions.memo: Clean homes stop germs from spreading and keep the family healthy. It also makes home a nicer place to be.

questions.question: Which one is a disease you can get from dirty water?
questions.ruby_prompt: Dirty water can make people sick. Which disease can come from it?
questions.expected: Diarrhoea
questions.memo: Drinking dirty water can give people diarrhoea (a sore tummy with watery stools). It can make children very weak, so safe water matters.

questions.question: Which one is keeping your environment clean?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one shows someone keeping the environment clean?
questions.context: Picture: a child picking up litter, a child throwing rubbish out of a car window, a child dropping a packet on the floor, a child kicking over a bin.
options: A child throwing rubbish from a car
A child dropping a packet on the floor
A child kicking over a bin
questions.expected: A child picking up litter
questions.memo: Picking up litter helps the place we live in. The other actions make the environment dirtier.

questions.question: Which insect can spread germs around food?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some insects spread germs to our food. Which one is a common one?
questions.expected: Flies
questions.memo: Flies land on dirty things and then on our food, leaving germs behind. Cover food and keep food areas clean to keep flies away.

questions.question: How does keeping the school toilets clean help everyone?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is it important that school toilets are clean?
options: It stops germs and diseases from spreading among learners
It makes them look pretty only
It is only for the cleaners' sake
questions.expected: It stops germs and diseases from spreading among learners
questions.memo: Toilets need to be clean because germs can spread fast and make many learners sick. Everyone helps by using them properly and flushing.

questions.question: Tuberculosis (TB) is spread by what?
questions.ruby_prompt: Tuberculosis (TB) is a serious illness. How does it spread?
options: Coughing and sneezing in the air
questions.expected: Coughing and sneezing in the air
questions.memo: TB spreads when sick people cough germs into the air. That is why we cover our mouths and seek treatment when we have a long cough.

questions.question: Put these litter-cleanup steps in the right order.
questions.ruby_prompt: Cleaning up litter is a kind thing to do. Put the steps in the right order.
options: Wear gloves or use a tool to pick up litter
Put the bag in a bin or recycling point
questions.expected: Wear gloves or use a tool to pick up litter,Collect litter into a bag,Put the bag in a bin or recycling point,Wash your hands afterwards
questions.memo: Cleaning up safely means protecting your hands first, collecting properly, throwing away in the right place, and washing your hands so germs don't spread.

questions.question: Why must we cover our food at home?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is it important to cover food at home?
options: To keep flies, dust and germs off it
questions.expected: To keep flies, dust and germs off it
questions.memo: Uncovered food collects flies and germs that can make us sick. Plates, lids and clingfilm all help keep food safe.

questions.question: Name one way you can help keep your school clean.
questions.ruby_prompt: Schools stay clean when everyone helps. Name one way you can help.
questions.expected: Pick up my own litter and put it in a bin
questions.memo: Many answers work — picking up litter, sweeping, using bins, not eating in the classroom, telling a teacher about mess.

questions.question: Which one is a healthy home environment?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one is a healthy home environment?
questions.context: Picture: a clean kitchen with food covered, an open bin with flies, dirty dishes left for days, a cracked toilet seat with smelly water.
options: A clean kitchen with food covered
A cracked toilet with smelly water
questions.expected: A clean kitchen with food covered
questions.memo: A healthy home has clean spaces and covered food. The other pictures show germ-friendly environments that can make families sick.

questions.question: Litter in the street can hurt animals.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Litter in the street can hurt animals.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — animals can eat plastic and get sick. Glass and tins can also cut them. Throwing rubbish in bins protects animals too.

questions.question: Why should we never burn rubbish near homes?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some people burn their rubbish, but it is not safe. Why not?
options: The smoke is harmful to breathe and can damage health
questions.expected: The smoke is harmful to breathe and can damage health
questions.memo: Burning rubbish — especially plastic — releases poisons into the air. The smoke can make people, especially children, cough and become sick.

questions.question: What can we do with peelings and food scraps to help the environment?
questions.ruby_prompt: Vegetable peelings and food scraps can be useful. What can we do with them?
options: Compost them to make fertiliser for plants
questions.expected: Compost them to make fertiliser for plants
questions.memo: Composting turns food scraps into rich soil. Many schools have compost heaps to grow gardens.

questions.question: Why should we wash our hands after picking up litter?
questions.ruby_prompt: After picking up litter, why is washing hands important?
options: Litter can have germs that make us sick
Hands are dirty just for fun
questions.expected: Litter can have germs that make us sick
questions.memo: Litter often carries germs. Washing afterwards stops the germs from going into our food or eyes.

LS.L2.BKH.T10.title: National symbols and the national anthem
LS.L2.BKH.T10.description: SA national symbols, currency, sports teams, holidays, flag, anthem, communicable diseases.
LS.L2.BKH.T10.recovery_strategy: Bring real items to the lesson if possible — a Rand coin, a printed flag, a recording of the anthem. Pride and recognition build with familiarity.

questions.question: What colours are on the South African flag?
questions.ruby_prompt: Our flag is special. What colours are on the South African flag?
options: Red, blue, green, white, yellow and black
questions.expected: Red, blue, green, white, yellow and black
questions.memo: The South African flag has six colours: red, blue, green, white, yellow and black. The Y-shape represents many paths joining together.

questions.question: What is our national anthem called?
questions.ruby_prompt: Every country has a national anthem. What is South Africa's called?
questions.expected: Nkosi Sikelel' iAfrika / Die Stem
questions.memo: Our national anthem combines parts of 'Nkosi Sikelel' iAfrika' and 'Die Stem' in five South African languages. It is sung at official events.

questions.question: What animal is on the South African coat of arms?
questions.ruby_prompt: Our coat of arms has animals on it. Which one?
questions.expected: A secretary bird
questions.memo: Our national bird, the secretary bird, is on the coat of arms with its wings spread. It is a strong African bird.

questions.question: Which one is South African money?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which money is used in South Africa?
questions.context: Picture: a Rand banknote, a US Dollar, a Euro, an Indian Rupee.
questions.expected: A Rand banknote
questions.memo: Our currency is the Rand. R10, R20, R50, R100 and R200 are common banknotes. R1, R2 and R5 are coins.

questions.question: When does South Africa celebrate Heritage Day?
questions.ruby_prompt: Heritage Day is a special South African holiday. Which month does it fall in?
questions.expected: September
questions.memo: Heritage Day is on 24 September. It celebrates all of South Africa's cultures and traditions. Many families have a braai together.

questions.question: South Africa has a national sports team called the Springboks.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? South Africa has a national rugby team called the Springboks.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — the Springboks are SA's national rugby team. South Africa also has Banyana Banyana (women's football), Bafana Bafana (men's football), and the Proteas (cricket).

questions.question: Which flower is the South African national flower?
questions.ruby_prompt: Our country has a national flower. Which one is it?
questions.expected: The King Protea
questions.memo: The King Protea is South Africa's national flower. It grows in the fynbos of the Cape and has a big, beautiful head.

questions.question: When South Africa won the Rugby World Cup, who was the team's captain?
questions.ruby_prompt: South Africa won the Rugby World Cup. A famous captain led the Springboks. Who?
questions.expected: Siya Kolisi
questions.memo: Siya Kolisi was the captain when the Springboks won the Rugby World Cup. He was the first black player to captain the team.

questions.question: Tell me one South African public holiday you know.
questions.ruby_prompt: South Africa has special public holidays. Tell me one you know.
questions.expected: Heritage Day
questions.memo: South African holidays include Heritage Day, Freedom Day, Workers' Day, Youth Day, Women's Day and others. Any one counts.

questions.question: What is on the front of most South African banknotes?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at a South African banknote. Whose face is on the front of most of them?
questions.expected: Nelson Mandela
questions.memo: Nelson Mandela's face is on R10, R20, R50, R100 and R200 banknotes. It honours his role in our democracy.

questions.question: How do we show respect during the national anthem?
questions.ruby_prompt: When the national anthem is sung at school, what do we do to show respect?
questions.expected: Stand quietly and sing along
questions.memo: Standing quietly shows respect for our country and the people who fought for our democracy. It is a small but important sign of pride.

questions.question: Put these South African currency values in order from smallest to largest.
questions.ruby_prompt: South African Rand coins and notes have different values. Put them from smallest to largest.
questions.expected: R1 coin,R10 note,R50 note,R100 note
questions.memo: Coins start small (R1), then notes go up — R10, R20, R50, R100, R200. Knowing money helps when shopping with family.

questions.question: Which national symbol grows in the SA bush and has a small striped face?
questions.ruby_prompt: Our national animal is a small striped grazing animal. Which one?
questions.expected: The springbok
questions.memo: The springbok is our national animal. It is also the name of our rugby team. Springboks are fast runners and great jumpers.

questions.question: Why are public holidays important?
questions.ruby_prompt: Public holidays are special. Why are they important?
options: They remind us of important events and people in our history
They are just days off for no reason
They are made to confuse us
questions.expected: They remind us of important events and people in our history
questions.memo: Holidays like Freedom Day or Heritage Day mark events that shaped South Africa. They help us remember and celebrate together.

questions.question: South Africa has only one official language.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? South Africa has only one official language.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: South Africa has 11 official languages, including isiZulu, English, Afrikaans, isiXhosa, Sesotho and more. We are a multilingual country.

LS.L2.BKH.T11.title: People at work
LS.L2.BKH.T11.description: Types of work, careers, protective clothing for different jobs.
LS.L2.BKH.T11.recovery_strategy: Anchor jobs to people the learner sees every day — the taxi driver, the spaza shopkeeper, the cleaner, the teacher. Then expand to less-visible careers.

questions.question: Which person needs to wear a hard hat at work?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some jobs need special hats for safety. Which job needs a hard hat?
options: A builder on a construction site
questions.expected: A builder on a construction site
questions.memo: Builders wear hard hats so that if something falls from above, their head is protected. Each job has its own safety clothing.

questions.question: Which job uses a sewing machine?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some jobs use a sewing machine. Which one?
questions.expected: A tailor or dressmaker
questions.memo: Tailors and dressmakers make clothes from cloth using sewing machines. Some adjust clothes that don't fit too.

questions.question: What does a doctor wear at work?
questions.ruby_prompt: Doctors often wear special clothes. What?
options: A white coat or scrubs and uses a stethoscope
questions.expected: A white coat or scrubs and uses a stethoscope
questions.memo: Doctors wear coats or scrubs to stay clean while seeing patients. The stethoscope lets them listen to hearts and lungs.

questions.question: Which one is a job people do at night?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some jobs happen mostly at night. Which one?
options: A bus driver only for school children
questions.expected: A security guard
questions.memo: Security guards often work at night to keep buildings and homes safe. Many people work while others sleep.

questions.question: What does a vet do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Vets are special doctors. Who do they treat?
options: Animals when they are sick or hurt
questions.expected: Animals when they are sick or hurt
questions.memo: A vet is a doctor for animals. They help pets, farm animals and sometimes wild animals get better.

questions.question: Which one is a person who grows food?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which person grows food?
questions.context: Picture: a farmer in a field, a banker in an office, a pilot in a plane, an actor on stage.
questions.expected: A farmer in a field
questions.memo: Farmers grow food on land — vegetables, fruits, grains. Without farmers, we would not have most of the food we eat.

questions.question: What is a 'career'?
questions.ruby_prompt: We often hear the word 'career'. What does it mean?
options: A type of work someone does for many years
questions.expected: A type of work someone does for many years
questions.memo: A career is the work someone does as their main job, often for many years. People train hard for their careers.

questions.question: Why do some workers wear gloves?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some workers wear gloves at work. Why?
options: To protect their hands from harm
questions.expected: To protect their hands from harm
questions.memo: Doctors wear gloves so germs don't spread. Builders wear gloves so they don't cut their hands. Each glove has a job to do.

questions.question: Which person helps you when you are very sick at the hospital?
questions.ruby_prompt: If you go to hospital, who helps you?
questions.expected: Doctors and nurses
questions.memo: Doctors and nurses work together at hospitals. Doctors find out what is wrong and nurses give care. Both are important.

questions.question: Tell me one job someone in your family does.
questions.ruby_prompt: People in our families work in many ways. Tell me one job a family member does.
questions.expected: My mum is a nurse
questions.memo: Family members work as teachers, nurses, drivers, cleaners, farmers, shopkeepers and more. All work is important.

questions.question: What does a mechanic do?
questions.ruby_prompt: If a car breaks down, who fixes it?
questions.expected: A mechanic
questions.memo: Mechanics know how cars work and fix them when they break. They use special tools and oil.

questions.question: Put these steps to becoming a doctor in order.
questions.ruby_prompt: Becoming a doctor takes many years. Put the steps in order.
options: Go to university to study medicine
questions.expected: Finish school,Go to university to study medicine,Train in a hospital,Start working as a doctor
questions.memo: Doctors finish school, study medicine for years at university, train in hospitals, and only then work as full doctors. It takes effort.

questions.question: Why is every job in a community important?
questions.ruby_prompt: From cleaners to doctors, every job matters. Why?
options: Each job keeps the community working well
questions.expected: Each job keeps the community working well
questions.memo: Without cleaners, places get dirty. Without drivers, people can't move. Every worker plays a part — that is why we respect everyone's job.

questions.question: Pilots fly aeroplanes.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Pilots fly aeroplanes.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — pilots are trained to fly aeroplanes safely. They take people from one airport to another.

questions.question: What job would you like to do when you grow up, and why?
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me about a job you might like to do when you grow up — and why.
questions.expected: I would like to be a teacher because I love helping people learn
questions.memo: Any job is welcome. Saying why helps you think about what you care about and what you might enjoy.

LS.L2.BKH.T12.title: The planets and the stars
LS.L2.BKH.T12.description: Solar system, planet names, sun and its uses, moon phases, space travel, sun protection.
LS.L2.BKH.T12.recovery_strategy: Help the learner look up at the sky. The moon and stars are right there for free. Real observation cements the names.

questions.question: What is the name of our planet?
questions.ruby_prompt: We live on a special planet. What is its name?
questions.expected: Earth
questions.memo: We live on Earth. It is the only planet in our solar system known to have life, with water, air, plants and animals.

questions.question: Which one is the closest star to Earth?
questions.ruby_prompt: Stars are far away — but one is much closer than the others. Which one?
questions.expected: The sun
questions.memo: The sun is a star — the closest one to Earth. It gives us light and warmth every day.

questions.question: The moon shines because...
questions.ruby_prompt: We can see the moon at night. Why does it shine?
options: It reflects light from the sun
It is made of glow-in-the-dark paint
It has a torch on it
questions.expected: It reflects light from the sun
questions.memo: The moon doesn't make its own light. The sun shines on the moon, and the moon bounces that light to us — that's why we see it.

questions.question: Put the moon phases in order.
questions.ruby_prompt: The moon changes shape over a month. Put the phases in order.
questions.expected: New moon (no moon visible),Half moon,Full moon,Half moon again
questions.memo: The moon goes from nothing visible (new), to half, to a full bright circle, and back to half before the next cycle. This takes about 29 days.

questions.question: Which one is a planet in our solar system?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the names. Which one is a planet?
questions.context: Picture: Jupiter, a moon, a star, a comet.
questions.expected: Jupiter
questions.memo: Jupiter is the biggest planet in our solar system. The Moon is not a planet (it orbits Earth), stars are like the sun, comets are icy travellers.

questions.question: Why do we need protection from the sun?
questions.ruby_prompt: The sun is good for us but can also hurt us. Why do we need protection from it?
options: Too much sun can burn skin and damage eyes
questions.expected: Too much sun can burn skin and damage eyes
questions.memo: Sun gives us light and warmth, but too much can sunburn skin and damage eyes. Hats, sunscreen and shade help.

questions.question: Which planet is known for its big ring?
questions.ruby_prompt: One planet has a very famous ring around it. Which one?
questions.expected: Saturn
questions.memo: Saturn has bright rings made of ice and dust. You can see them through a telescope.

questions.question: Astronauts are people who travel into space.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Astronauts are people who travel into space.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — astronauts train for years and travel into space in rockets. They have visited the moon and live for months on a space station.

questions.question: What lives on Earth that does not live on other planets we know of?
questions.ruby_prompt: Earth is special. What is on Earth that we have not found on other planets yet?
options: Plants, animals and people — life itself
questions.expected: Plants, animals and people — life itself
questions.memo: As far as we know, Earth is the only planet with living things. That is why we care for our planet — there isn't another like it.

questions.question: Name one thing the sun helps us with on Earth.
questions.ruby_prompt: The sun helps Earth in many ways. Name one.
questions.expected: The sun gives us light and warmth
questions.memo: The sun gives light, warmth, helps plants grow, dries our washing, and powers solar panels. There are many right answers.

questions.question: Which planet is closest to the sun?
questions.ruby_prompt: The planets are arranged at different distances from the sun. Which one is closest?
questions.expected: Mercury
questions.memo: Mercury is the smallest planet and closest to the sun. It is very hot during the day and very cold at night.

questions.question: Which is dangerous to do — and not necessary — when looking at the sky?
questions.ruby_prompt: When looking at the sky, what is dangerous to do?
questions.expected: Look directly at the sun
questions.memo: Looking straight at the sun can damage your eyes for ever, even for a short moment. Never look directly at it.

questions.question: What is a 'galaxy'?
questions.ruby_prompt: Astronomers talk about galaxies. What is a galaxy?
options: A huge group of stars and planets
questions.expected: A huge group of stars and planets
questions.memo: A galaxy holds billions of stars. Our sun is one star in the Milky Way galaxy. There are countless galaxies in the universe.

questions.question: Which one is a man-made object that orbits Earth?
questions.ruby_prompt: People have built things that orbit our planet. Which is one?
questions.expected: A satellite
questions.memo: Satellites are built by people and sent into space. They help us with TV, weather forecasts and cellphone signals.

questions.question: Tell me one thing you would like to know about space.
questions.ruby_prompt: Space is full of mysteries. Tell me one thing you would like to know about space.
questions.expected: How long it takes to fly to Mars
questions.memo: Curiosity is how astronauts and scientists start. Any wondering counts.

LS.L3.BKH.T01.title: Clothes and the materials they are made from
LS.L3.BKH.T01.description: Clothing categories, materials, processing, cultural and seasonal clothing, protective wear, clothing care.
LS.L3.BKH.T01.recovery_strategy: Bring real fabric samples or use the learner's own clothing as a teaching tool. Touching cotton, wool and synthetic helps the words stick.

questions.question: What material is most cotton clothing made from?
questions.ruby_prompt: Cotton T-shirts are very common. What material is cotton made from?
options: A plant that grows fluffy white fibres
questions.expected: A plant that grows fluffy white fibres
questions.memo: Cotton comes from the cotton plant. The fluffy white tufts are spun into thread, which is woven into fabric for T-shirts, jeans and more.

questions.question: Wool comes from which animal?
questions.ruby_prompt: Wool keeps us warm in winter. Which animal does it come from?
questions.expected: Sheep
questions.memo: Sheep grow thick wool, which farmers cut once a year. The wool is then spun into yarn for jerseys, scarves and blankets.

questions.question: Which type of clothing is best for a very cold winter day?
questions.ruby_prompt: On a cold winter morning, what kind of clothing keeps you warmest?
options: A thick wool jersey, scarf and hat
questions.expected: A thick wool jersey, scarf and hat
questions.memo: Layers trap warm air close to your body. A jersey, scarf and hat protect chest, neck and head from cold.

questions.question: Why do firefighters wear special protective clothing?
questions.ruby_prompt: Firefighters wear thick suits. Why?
options: To protect them from heat, flames and smoke
questions.expected: To protect them from heat, flames and smoke
questions.memo: Firefighter suits are made of fire-resistant material with a helmet, gloves and boots. Without this gear they could be badly burned.

questions.question: What is a 'traditional outfit'?
questions.ruby_prompt: We talk about traditional outfits at Heritage Day. What is a traditional outfit?
options: Clothing that comes from a particular culture and is often worn for special occasions
questions.expected: Clothing that comes from a particular culture and is often worn for special occasions
questions.memo: Traditional outfits — like isiZulu, isiXhosa, Sotho, Indian sari, or Cape Malay clothes — show culture and history. Many SA families have them for weddings or Heritage Day.

questions.question: Put the steps of making a cotton T-shirt in order.
questions.ruby_prompt: A T-shirt has a long journey. Put the steps in order.
options: Cotton plants are grown on a farm
Fabric is cut and sewn into a T-shirt
questions.expected: Cotton plants are grown on a farm,Cotton is spun into thread,Thread is woven into fabric,Fabric is cut and sewn into a T-shirt
questions.memo: Clothes start in nature. From plant to thread to fabric to finished clothing — each step transforms the material.

questions.question: Which one is a synthetic (man-made) material?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some materials are natural and some are man-made. Which one is man-made?
questions.expected: Polyester
questions.memo: Polyester is made in factories from chemicals. Cotton, wool and silk all come from plants or animals.

questions.question: Why do construction workers wear high-visibility (bright yellow or orange) jackets?
questions.ruby_prompt: Workers near roads wear bright orange or yellow jackets. Why?
options: So drivers can see them easily and not hit them
questions.expected: So drivers can see them easily and not hit them
questions.memo: Bright colours and reflective strips help drivers spot workers from far away, day or night. This is life-saving safety clothing.

questions.question: Which one shows traditional South African clothing?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one shows traditional South African clothing?
questions.context: Picture: a Zulu woman in beaded traditional dress, a tracksuit, a swimsuit, a business suit.
options: A Zulu woman in beaded traditional dress
questions.expected: A Zulu woman in beaded traditional dress
questions.memo: Traditional Zulu beadwork is a rich part of South African culture. Each colour and pattern carries meaning.

questions.question: How should you wash dirty clothes?
questions.ruby_prompt: Clothes get dirty. How should we wash them?
options: With water and soap, then rinse and dry
Put them in the sun for a moment
questions.expected: With water and soap, then rinse and dry
questions.memo: Washing with soap and water removes dirt and germs. Drying in the sun makes them fresh. Clean clothes keep us healthy.

questions.question: Tell me about an item of clothing that is special to you or your family.
questions.ruby_prompt: Some clothes are special. Tell me about one that matters to your family.
questions.expected: My grandmother's wedding dress
questions.memo: Family clothes often carry stories — weddings, traditions, gifts. Sharing them helps us understand each other.

questions.question: Why do some workers wear closed safety shoes with hard toes?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some workers wear special hard-toe boots. Why?
options: To protect their feet if heavy things fall on them
questions.expected: To protect their feet if heavy things fall on them
questions.memo: Workers in factories, mines and on building sites need protected feet. The hard cap inside the boot stops serious injuries.

questions.question: Which clothing item is worn to protect the head from the sun?
questions.ruby_prompt: On a sunny day, what helps protect your head?
questions.expected: A wide-brim hat
questions.memo: A wide-brim hat shades your face and neck from the sun. Sun on your face for too long can cause sunburn and, later, skin damage.

questions.question: Cotton comes from a plant.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Cotton comes from a plant.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — cotton grows on cotton plants. The fluffy white tufts are picked, cleaned, and spun into thread.

questions.question: Why do hospital nurses and doctors wear scrubs?
questions.ruby_prompt: Hospital staff wear blue or green scrubs. Why?
options: Scrubs are easy to wash and keep germs out of clothes from home
questions.expected: Scrubs are easy to wash and keep germs out of clothes from home
questions.memo: Scrubs are cleaned at the hospital so staff don't bring germs from home or take them home. Hygiene is a key safety practice.

questions.question: Put these clothing-care steps in order.
questions.ruby_prompt: Looking after clothes makes them last longer. Put the steps in order.
options: Hang to dry in the sun
questions.expected: Sort dark clothes from light,Wash with soap and water,Hang to dry in the sun,Fold and put away
questions.memo: Sorting stops colours running into each other. Washing cleans, drying fresh, folding makes them ready for next time.

questions.question: What kind of clothing would you wear to a friend's wedding?
questions.ruby_prompt: You are invited to a friend's family wedding. What kind of clothes might you wear?
options: Smart formal clothes or your traditional outfit
questions.expected: Smart formal clothes or your traditional outfit
questions.memo: Weddings are special occasions where people dress in their best. Traditional or smart clothes show respect for the family.

questions.question: Why is it good to mend clothes instead of throwing them away?
questions.ruby_prompt: When a small hole appears in clothes, why is it good to mend it?
options: It saves money and reduces waste
It is bad for the environment
questions.expected: It saves money and reduces waste
questions.memo: Mending small tears costs less than buying new. It also keeps clothes out of landfill and reduces waste — good for the planet.

questions.question: Name one type of protective clothing and a worker who uses it.
questions.ruby_prompt: Protective clothing keeps workers safe. Name one type and who uses it.
questions.expected: A hard hat for builders
questions.memo: Hard hats for builders, gloves for doctors, gowns and aprons for chefs, helmets for cyclists, life jackets for sailors — many right answers.

questions.question: Hot countries near the equator often have lighter, looser clothing.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Hot countries near the equator often have lighter, looser clothing.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — loose, light clothes let air flow and protect from the sun. In cold countries, people wear heavy, layered clothes instead.

LS.L3.BKH.T02.title: Farming the land
LS.L3.BKH.T02.description: Farm-grown foods, home garden, food production processes, staple foods, healthy eating.
LS.L3.BKH.T02.recovery_strategy: Visit a real garden or food market if possible. Watching food grow or seeing where it comes from sticks better than diagrams.

questions.question: Which food grows under the ground?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some foods grow under the soil. Which one is one of them?
questions.expected: Potatoes
questions.memo: Potatoes grow under the ground as part of the plant's roots. Apples and pineapples grow on plants above the soil.

questions.question: Which food is a staple food in many South African homes?
questions.ruby_prompt: A staple food is one people eat almost every day. Which is a SA staple?
questions.expected: Maize (mealies/pap)
questions.memo: Maize is the most important staple food in South Africa. It is made into pap, porridge and samp — affordable and filling.

questions.question: What is needed for a vegetable garden to grow well?
questions.ruby_prompt: If you want vegetables in a garden, what do they need?
questions.expected: Sunlight, water, soil and seeds
questions.memo: Plants need light to make food, water to grow, soil to root in, and seeds to start. With these four, almost anything can grow.

questions.question: Where does bread start its journey?
questions.ruby_prompt: Bread doesn't appear by magic. Where does its journey start?
questions.expected: On a wheat farm
questions.memo: Wheat is grown on farms. The seeds are ground into flour, mixed into dough, baked into bread, and reach our tables.

questions.question: Why do farmers rotate which crops they plant?
questions.ruby_prompt: Smart farmers plant different crops in different seasons. Why?
options: To keep the soil healthy and full of goodness
questions.expected: To keep the soil healthy and full of goodness
questions.memo: Different plants take different things from the soil. Rotating crops gives the soil time to recover its nutrients.

questions.question: Put the stages of growing a maize plant in order.
questions.ruby_prompt: Maize takes time to grow. Put the stages in order.
questions.expected: Seed planted in the soil,Small green shoot appears,Tall stalk grows with leaves,Maize cobs form
questions.memo: From a tiny seed to a tall stalk with cobs takes weeks of sunshine and rain. Farmers wait patiently between planting and harvest.

questions.question: Which is a healthy plate of food?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one is a healthy plate of food?
questions.context: Picture: pap with vegetables and chicken, just sweets, just chips, just a fizzy drink.
questions.expected: Pap with vegetables and chicken
questions.memo: A balanced meal has a grain (pap), vegetables and a protein (chicken). That gives your body everything it needs.

questions.question: What is 'subsistence farming'?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some families farm just to feed themselves. What is that called?
options: Growing food mainly for your own family to eat
Growing food only to sell to shops
questions.expected: Growing food mainly for your own family to eat
questions.memo: Many South African families have small gardens to feed themselves. It is called subsistence farming when most of what you grow you eat.

questions.question: Why is it good to eat fruit and vegetables every day?
questions.ruby_prompt: Doctors say we should eat fruit and vegetables every day. Why?
options: They give us vitamins, fibre and energy to grow
questions.expected: They give us vitamins, fibre and energy to grow
questions.memo: Fruit and vegetables are packed with vitamins that help our bodies fight illness and grow strong. We should eat them every day.

questions.question: What is the difference between a farm and an orchard?
questions.ruby_prompt: Both farms and orchards grow food. What is the difference?
options: Orchards mainly grow fruit trees, farms grow many crops or keep animals
questions.expected: Orchards mainly grow fruit trees, farms grow many crops or keep animals
questions.memo: Orchards are full of fruit trees — apples, peaches, plums. Farms are bigger and grow many crops or raise animals like cows and sheep.

questions.question: Name one fruit or vegetable that grows in South Africa.
questions.ruby_prompt: South Africa grows many lovely fruits and vegetables. Name one.
questions.expected: Oranges grown in the Eastern Cape
questions.memo: SA grows oranges, apples, peaches, grapes, avocados, mangoes, pumpkins, spinach, potatoes — many great answers.

questions.question: What is samp?
questions.ruby_prompt: Samp is a traditional South African food. What is it?
options: Crushed dried maize, often eaten with beans
questions.expected: Crushed dried maize, often eaten with beans
questions.memo: Samp is made from dry maize that's been broken into small pieces. It is filling, healthy, and often cooked with beans.

questions.question: A garden needs water every day in very hot, dry weather.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? A garden needs water every day in very hot, dry weather.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: In dry weather, plants can dry out fast. Watering daily (early morning is best) keeps them alive. But we still want to save water by watering only the plants, not the path.

questions.question: Why is it healthier to eat fresh food than packaged junk food?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why do nutrition experts say fresh food is healthier than packaged junk food?
options: Fresh food has more vitamins and less salt, sugar and fat
Packaged food gives more energy for sport
questions.expected: Fresh food has more vitamins and less salt, sugar and fat
questions.memo: Fresh food is closer to nature — more vitamins and minerals, less added salt, sugar and fat. Junk food fills us up but does not feed our bodies well.

questions.question: Which animal is kept on farms to give us milk?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which farm animal gives us most of the milk we drink?
questions.expected: Cows
questions.memo: Cows give most of the milk we drink. Goats are kept by some families too. Chickens, pigs and fish do not give milk.

questions.question: What is a 'crop'?
questions.ruby_prompt: Farmers talk about their 'crops'. What is a crop?
options: A plant grown in large amounts for food
questions.expected: A plant grown in large amounts for food
questions.memo: A crop is a plant grown by farmers for food, like maize, wheat or sugar cane. The word can also be used for cotton or other useful plants.

questions.question: Why do farmers depend on rain?
questions.ruby_prompt: Farmers watch the weather closely. Why do they depend on rain?
options: Crops need water to grow and rain is the main natural source
questions.expected: Crops need water to grow and rain is the main natural source
questions.memo: Without enough rain, crops fail. That is why droughts (long dry times) are so hard for farmers and food prices in shops.
