questions.question: Which is a vegetable that often grows in South African gardens?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which vegetable often grows in SA gardens?
questions.context: Picture: spinach (morogo), a pineapple, an ice cream, a chocolate bar.
questions.expected: Spinach (morogo)
questions.memo: Morogo (wild spinach) grows easily in SA gardens and is full of vitamins. Pineapples grow on big farms in warm areas, not most home gardens.

questions.question: Tell me one food from South Africa and where it might be grown.
questions.ruby_prompt: South Africa grows many foods. Tell me one and where it might be grown.
questions.expected: Oranges grow in the Eastern Cape
questions.memo: Examples: oranges in the Eastern Cape, apples in Ceres, sugar in KwaZulu-Natal, maize in the Free State. Many right answers.

questions.question: Eating only sweets and crisps for lunch every day is healthy.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Eating only sweets and crisps for lunch every day is healthy.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Sweets and crisps have a lot of sugar, salt and fat. Eating only these means our bodies don't get the vitamins they need.

LS.L3.BKH.T03.title: Extinct and endangered creatures
LS.L3.BKH.T03.description: Dinosaur age, kinds of dinosaurs, how species become extinct, endangered animals, safety with sharp objects.
LS.L3.BKH.T03.recovery_strategy: Use real images and child-friendly facts about dinosaurs and endangered animals. Curiosity is the strongest driver — let learners ask questions.

questions.question: What is a 'dinosaur'?
questions.ruby_prompt: Dinosaurs are famous animals. What were they?
options: Animals that lived on Earth millions of years ago and no longer exist
Animals that live in zoos today
A type of bird that flies fast
questions.expected: Animals that lived on Earth millions of years ago and no longer exist
questions.memo: Dinosaurs roamed Earth millions of years ago. They went extinct long before people lived. We learn about them from fossils.

questions.question: What does 'extinct' mean?
questions.ruby_prompt: We say dinosaurs are extinct. What does extinct mean?
options: No longer alive anywhere on Earth
questions.expected: No longer alive anywhere on Earth
questions.memo: Extinct means a kind of animal or plant has died out completely. Once a species is extinct, it cannot come back.

questions.question: What does 'endangered' mean?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some animals today are 'endangered'. What does that mean?
options: So few are left that they could become extinct
questions.expected: So few are left that they could become extinct
questions.memo: Endangered species are at risk of disappearing forever. We work hard to protect them so they don't become extinct.

questions.question: Which famous SA animal is endangered because of poaching?
questions.ruby_prompt: Poachers hunt one big SA animal for its horn. Which one is endangered because of this?
questions.expected: The rhino
questions.memo: Rhinos are killed by poachers who want their horns. South Africa works hard to protect rhinos in reserves with rangers.

questions.question: Where do scientists find dinosaur bones?
questions.ruby_prompt: Scientists dig up dinosaur bones. Where do they find them?
options: Buried in layers of rock and soil
In a cupboard at the museum
questions.expected: Buried in layers of rock and soil
questions.memo: Dinosaur bones become fossils after millions of years buried in rock. Scientists called palaeontologists carefully dig them up.

questions.question: Which dinosaur ate plants?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some dinosaurs ate plants and some ate meat. Which one ate plants?
questions.expected: Brachiosaurus (long-necked plant eater)
questions.memo: Brachiosaurus had a long neck to reach high leaves. T-rex and others had sharp teeth and claws for hunting meat.

questions.question: What likely caused most dinosaurs to go extinct?
questions.ruby_prompt: Scientists have a leading idea about what caused the dinosaurs to die out. What was it?
options: A huge asteroid crashed into Earth and changed the climate
They all ate too many sweets
questions.expected: A huge asteroid crashed into Earth and changed the climate
questions.memo: Most scientists believe a massive asteroid hit Earth long ago, blocking out the sun and changing the weather. Most dinosaurs could not survive.

questions.question: Why are some sea animals endangered?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some sea animals are in trouble. Why are some endangered?
options: Plastic pollution, overfishing and warming oceans
questions.expected: Plastic pollution, overfishing and warming oceans
questions.memo: Sea turtles eat plastic bags thinking they are jellyfish. Fish get caught faster than they can reproduce. Warmer water hurts coral. All these threaten sea life.

questions.question: Which is a sign that an animal might be a fossil?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which is a fossil?
questions.context: Picture: a dinosaur footprint in rock, a paper drawing, a wooden chair, a glass bottle.
questions.expected: A dinosaur footprint in rock
questions.memo: Fossils are remains or marks of ancient living things preserved in rock — bones, shells, footprints. They teach us about the past.

questions.question: Name one endangered animal in South Africa.
questions.ruby_prompt: South Africa has several endangered animals. Name one.
questions.expected: The rhino
questions.memo: Endangered SA animals include the black rhino, African wild dog, riverine rabbit, blue crane and many sea creatures. Any one is valid.

questions.question: Why must we use sharp scissors and knives carefully?
questions.ruby_prompt: We sometimes use sharp tools in class. Why must we be careful?
options: They can cut skin and cause serious harm if mishandled
questions.expected: They can cut skin and cause serious harm if mishandled
questions.memo: Sharp tools cut things — including fingers. Use the right way, point away from your body, and stop if you are tired or distracted.

questions.question: Which is a safety rule for using scissors?
questions.ruby_prompt: Scissors are useful but can hurt. Which is a safety rule?
options: Pass scissors with the closed blades pointing down, handle first
questions.expected: Pass scissors with the closed blades pointing down, handle first
questions.memo: Passing scissors handle-first means the blades can't accidentally cut. Running with scissors is one of the most dangerous things — never do it.

questions.question: What can we do to help protect endangered animals?
questions.ruby_prompt: Children can help save endangered animals. What can we do?
options: Support conservation groups, never buy items from poachers, and tell others
questions.expected: Support conservation groups, never buy items from poachers, and tell others
questions.memo: Even small actions matter. Talking about endangered animals, refusing to buy illegal animal products, and supporting reserves all help.

questions.question: How long ago did dinosaurs live?
questions.ruby_prompt: Dinosaurs lived a really, really long time ago. About how long ago?
questions.expected: Millions of years ago
questions.memo: Dinosaurs lived between about 65 million and 230 million years ago. That is many millions of years before humans existed.

questions.question: Birds are related to dinosaurs.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Birds are related to dinosaurs.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — scientists believe modern birds are the descendants of certain small feathered dinosaurs. So when you see a chicken, you're looking at a dinosaur cousin.

questions.question: Why is it important to protect animal habitats?
questions.ruby_prompt: Habitats are where animals live. Why must we protect them?
options: Without their home, animals cannot survive
questions.expected: Without their home, animals cannot survive
questions.memo: When forests are cut down or wetlands drained, the animals there lose their home and food. Protecting habitats protects all the species that live in them.

questions.question: Which one is an animal that has been extinct for a long time?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some animals have been gone for a very long time. Which one?
questions.expected: The dodo bird
questions.memo: The dodo was a flightless bird that lived on the island of Mauritius. It went extinct hundreds of years ago after humans arrived.

questions.question: Put these steps for safely passing scissors in order.
questions.ruby_prompt: Passing scissors safely takes practice. Put the steps in order.
options: Hold the closed blades in your hand
Offer the handle to your friend
Let go once they have a firm grip
questions.expected: Close the blades,Hold the closed blades in your hand,Offer the handle to your friend,Let go once they have a firm grip
questions.memo: Close, hold, offer handle, release. This sequence keeps the sharp parts away from the receiver every step of the way.

questions.question: Tell me one fact about a dinosaur or extinct animal you find interesting.
questions.ruby_prompt: Extinct animals are fascinating. Tell me one fact you find interesting.
questions.expected: The T-rex had very small arms
questions.memo: Any real interest counts — sizes, food, where they lived. Curiosity is how scientists discover more.

questions.question: If you find what looks like a fossil while playing, what should you do?
questions.ruby_prompt: You think you've found a fossil while playing. What should you do?
options: Show a grown-up — it might be important
Smash it open to look inside
questions.expected: Show a grown-up — it might be important
questions.memo: Real fossils are valuable for science and shouldn't be damaged. A grown-up can ask a museum if they want to look at it.

LS.L3.BKH.T04.title: Communication then and now
LS.L3.BKH.T04.description: Communication history, radio/telegraph/TV/newspapers, modern communication (SMS, email, internet), safety with media.
LS.L3.BKH.T04.recovery_strategy: Bring in old letters or stamps if you can. Compare with a smartphone the learner knows. The contrast makes the history real.

questions.question: How did people send messages before phones existed?
questions.ruby_prompt: Long before cellphones, how did people send messages?
questions.expected: Hand-written letters through the post
questions.memo: Before phones and the internet, letters were the main way to send messages. They could take days or weeks to travel.

questions.question: What is a 'newspaper'?
questions.ruby_prompt: We hear about newspapers. What is one?
options: A printed paper with daily news
A type of book about animals
questions.expected: A printed paper with daily news
questions.memo: Newspapers print fresh news every day or every week — politics, sports, weather. Today many newspapers are also online.

questions.question: What does 'SMS' stand for?
questions.ruby_prompt: We often see 'SMS' on cellphones. What does it mean?
options: Short Message Service — a text on your phone
questions.expected: Short Message Service — a text on your phone
questions.memo: SMS means Short Message Service. It's the short text messages sent from one cellphone to another.

questions.question: What is the internet?
questions.ruby_prompt: We use the word 'internet' a lot. What is it?
options: A network connecting computers and phones around the world
questions.expected: A network connecting computers and phones around the world
questions.memo: The internet is a giant web of computers all over the world. It lets us share messages, photos, videos and information almost instantly.

questions.question: Put these communication tools in order from oldest to newest.
questions.ruby_prompt: Communication has changed over time. Put these in order from oldest to newest.
questions.expected: Hand-written letters,Telegraph,Telephone (landline),Cellphones with internet
questions.memo: Letters were ancient. Telegraphs sent dot-dash messages long ago. Then telephones with cables. Then mobile phones with internet — each newer.

questions.question: Why do TV shows have age restrictions like 'PG' or '13+'?
questions.ruby_prompt: TV shows sometimes have 'PG' or '13+' on them. Why?
options: To show whether the content is suitable for children
questions.expected: To show whether the content is suitable for children
questions.memo: Age restrictions warn parents and children that some content (violence, scary scenes, adult themes) may not be suitable for young viewers.

questions.question: Which is older — a telephone or an email?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which one came first — the telephone or email?
options: They came at the same time
questions.expected: The telephone
questions.memo: Telephones were invented in the 1870s. Email was created over 100 years later in the 1970s and became common in the 1990s.

questions.question: Why is it important to tell a grown-up if a stranger online asks for personal information?
questions.ruby_prompt: If a stranger on the internet asks where you live or your school name, what should you do?
options: Tell a parent or trusted grown-up — don't share personal information
questions.expected: Tell a parent or trusted grown-up — don't share personal information
questions.memo: Online strangers can pretend to be anyone. Never share where you live, your school, your photo, or your name with strangers. Always tell a trusted grown-up.

questions.question: Which one is a way to communicate today?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one is a way to communicate today?
questions.context: Picture: a smartphone with messages, a pair of shoes, a stick, an apple.
questions.expected: A smartphone with messages
questions.memo: Smartphones can send texts, make calls, send video, and email. They are powerful communication tools.

questions.question: What is a radio?
questions.ruby_prompt: Radios have been around a long time. What is a radio?
options: A device that receives broadcasts of music, news and talk
questions.expected: A device that receives broadcasts of music, news and talk
questions.memo: Radios pick up signals from broadcasting stations. They have been important for news, music and stories for over 100 years.

questions.question: What does it mean to 'go viral' on the internet?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sometimes a video 'goes viral'. What does that mean?
options: Many, many people share it in a short time
It has a real virus inside
questions.expected: Many, many people share it in a short time
questions.memo: Going viral means spreading quickly across many people online. The word comes from how a virus spreads — but here it's just a video or post.

questions.question: Tell me about one way you talk to family members who live far away.
questions.ruby_prompt: If you have family far away, how do you stay in touch?
questions.expected: We call on the phone or send WhatsApp messages
questions.memo: Phone calls, WhatsApp, video calls, emails, letters — all are ways to keep in touch. Any answer counts.

questions.question: Why must we be careful about what we read online?
questions.ruby_prompt: Not everything on the internet is true. Why must we be careful?
options: Some information is made up or wrong
questions.expected: Some information is made up or wrong
questions.memo: Anyone can put things online. Some posts are wrong on purpose (lies) or by mistake. Check with a trusted source — a teacher, parent, or proper website.

questions.question: Books, radio and TV are all examples of media.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Books, radio and TV are all examples of media.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — media is anything that carries information to many people. Books, radio, TV, newspapers and the internet are all media.

questions.question: If a friend sends you a mean message online, what should you do?
questions.ruby_prompt: A friend sends you a mean message online. What is the best thing to do?
options: Tell a parent or teacher — save the message as evidence
questions.expected: Tell a parent or teacher — save the message as evidence
questions.memo: Cyberbullying is real bullying. Trusted grown-ups can help stop it and talk with the other family if needed. You are never alone in this.

questions.question: What did people use before colour TV?
questions.ruby_prompt: Before colour TV, what kind of TV did people watch?
questions.expected: Black-and-white television
questions.memo: Early TVs only showed black and white. Colour TV became common from the 1960s and 1970s. Some grandparents remember the change well.

questions.question: Why is too much screen time not healthy for children?
questions.ruby_prompt: Doctors say children should not spend all day on screens. Why?
options: It can hurt eyes, sleep, and stop you being active outdoors
It is healthy in any amount
questions.expected: It can hurt eyes, sleep, and stop you being active outdoors
questions.memo: Too much screen time can strain eyes, make sleep worse, and replace active play. Balance is the key — screens are okay, but not all the time.

questions.question: Which one is a community newspaper for?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some small newspapers cover only one town or area. What are they for?
options: Sharing news that matters to people in that community
questions.expected: Sharing news that matters to people in that community
questions.memo: Community newspapers cover local stories — school events, council news, local sports. They are an important way neighbourhoods stay informed.

questions.question: Name one way you could share important news with your whole class today.
questions.ruby_prompt: If you had important news to share with the whole class, how could you do it?
questions.expected: Make an announcement during morning circle
questions.memo: Many right answers — a poster, a class WhatsApp message via the teacher, an announcement, a song or play. Good communication finds the right tool.

questions.question: Sharing your home address with a stranger online is safe.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Sharing your home address with a stranger online is safe.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Sharing your address with strangers online is very dangerous. Keep personal information private and tell a trusted grown-up if anyone asks.

LS.L3.BKH.T05.title: Communicable diseases
LS.L3.BKH.T05.description: Communicable diseases (HIV/AIDS, flu, cholera, measles, TB), causes, prevention, symptoms, treatment, caring for sick family, coping with grief and loss. SENSITIVE — handle with care.
LS.L3.BKH.T05.recovery_strategy: This topic touches on illness, HIV/AIDS, and grief — handle slowly and gently. Lead with the truth that many illnesses can be prevented or treated, and that asking for help from a trusted grown-up is always the right thing. If a learner is grieving, prioritise comfort over content.

questions.question: What is a 'communicable' disease?
questions.ruby_prompt: We hear the word 'communicable disease' a lot. What does it mean?
options: A disease that can spread from one person to another
A disease that only one person can ever have
questions.expected: A disease that can spread from one person to another
questions.memo: Communicable diseases spread between people through germs in the air, on hands, or in body fluids. Colds, flu and TB are common examples.

questions.question: How does the flu mostly spread between people?
questions.ruby_prompt: When someone has the flu, how does it spread to other people?
options: Through coughs, sneezes and touching shared surfaces
questions.expected: Through coughs, sneezes and touching shared surfaces
questions.memo: Flu germs travel in the tiny droplets we sneeze and cough out. Covering your mouth and washing hands stops the spread.

questions.question: What does HIV/AIDS stand for at the simplest level?
questions.ruby_prompt: HIV/AIDS is a serious illness. What does the term mean in simple words?
options: A virus that weakens the body's defences, with treatment available today
questions.expected: A virus that weakens the body's defences, with treatment available today
questions.memo: HIV is a virus that makes it harder for the body to fight illness. Thanks to medicine (called ARVs), many people living with HIV today live long, healthy lives.

questions.question: Is HIV spread through ordinary touch, like hugs or sharing food?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some people worry about hugging or sharing food with a friend who has HIV. Is HIV spread that way?
options: No — HIV is not spread by hugs, sharing food, or playing together
Yes, by every kind of touch
questions.expected: No — HIV is not spread by hugs, sharing food, or playing together
questions.memo: You cannot get HIV from hugs, sharing food, sharing toys, or being in the same room. Knowing this protects friends with HIV from being treated unfairly.

questions.question: Why is it kind to be friendly to someone living with HIV?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some children at school may have HIV. Why is it kind to be a normal friend to them?
options: They are children just like us and deserve kindness
questions.expected: They are children just like us and deserve kindness
questions.memo: Children with HIV go to school, play and learn like everyone else. With their medicine they are healthy. Friendship and kindness matter.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop a cold from spreading in your home?
questions.ruby_prompt: If someone in your home has a cold, what helps stop it spreading?
options: Cover coughs, wash hands often, don't share cups
questions.expected: Cover coughs, wash hands often, don't share cups
questions.memo: Simple habits stop germs spreading at home — covering coughs, washing hands, not sharing things that touch the mouth.

questions.question: Tuberculosis (TB) is a serious lung disease. How is it usually treated?
questions.ruby_prompt: TB is a serious illness, but it can be treated. How?
options: With medicine prescribed by a clinic or doctor — taken every day until finished
By staying outside in the cold
questions.expected: With medicine prescribed by a clinic or doctor — taken every day until finished
questions.memo: TB needs medicine from a clinic, taken every day for many months. Finishing the full course is essential — stopping early can let it come back stronger.

questions.question: If someone in your family is sick, how can you help?
questions.ruby_prompt: When a family member is sick, how can a child help in small ways?
options: Bring them water, be quiet near them, and tell a grown-up if they need more help
questions.expected: Bring them water, be quiet near them, and tell a grown-up if they need more help
questions.memo: Small acts of kindness — water, a quiet room, a hug if they want one — help sick family members feel cared for. Grown-ups handle the medicine.

questions.question: Why do we never share needles or anything sharp that has blood on it?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why must we never share needles or anything sharp with blood on it?
options: Blood can carry diseases like HIV from one person to another
questions.expected: Blood can carry diseases like HIV from one person to another
questions.memo: Sharing anything with blood on it can pass diseases between people. If you see a needle, never pick it up — tell a grown-up.

questions.question: If you lose someone you love, it is okay to feel sad for a long time.
questions.ruby_prompt: When we lose someone we love, big feelings can stay a long time. Is it okay?
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Grief is love that has nowhere to go. Sad feelings come and go for a long time, and that is normal. There is no right way to grieve.

questions.question: When you feel sad about losing someone, what is one helpful thing to do?
questions.ruby_prompt: When you feel sad about losing someone, what can help?
options: Talk to a parent, teacher, or other trusted grown-up
Keep all the sadness inside forever
questions.expected: Talk to a parent, teacher, or other trusted grown-up
questions.memo: Trusted grown-ups can listen, share memories, and help carry the heavy feelings. You are never being a burden by talking. ChildLine (116) is also free if you need it.

questions.question: Tell me one kind thing you could do for a friend who has lost someone they love.
questions.ruby_prompt: A friend has lost someone they love. Tell me one kind thing you could do.
questions.expected: Sit with them and listen if they want to talk
questions.memo: Just being there matters. A hug, listening, a kind note, or sitting in silence — all are kind. You don't need fancy words.

questions.question: Why is sleeping under a mosquito net important in malaria areas?
questions.ruby_prompt: In areas where there is malaria, why do families use mosquito nets at night?
options: Mosquitoes can carry malaria — the net keeps them off you while you sleep
questions.expected: Mosquitoes can carry malaria — the net keeps them off you while you sleep
questions.memo: Malaria is spread by certain mosquitoes that bite at night. A treated net is one of the best ways to stay safe in affected areas.

questions.question: Vaccines (injections) help our bodies fight diseases.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Vaccines (injections at the clinic) help our bodies fight diseases.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — vaccines teach your body how to fight germs without you getting sick first. They have saved millions of lives.

questions.question: Cholera spreads mostly through what?
questions.ruby_prompt: Cholera is a disease that has caused outbreaks in SA. How does it mostly spread?
questions.expected: Dirty water and unwashed food
questions.memo: Cholera spreads through water and food contaminated by sewage. Clean water and good hygiene stop it.

questions.question: What should you do if you have a long cough that does not go away?
questions.ruby_prompt: A cough that lasts many weeks can be a sign of something serious. What should you do?
options: Visit the clinic to get checked
Run more to make it stop
questions.expected: Visit the clinic to get checked
questions.memo: A long cough can be TB or something else needing treatment. Clinics test for free and can prescribe the right medicine.

questions.question: Which one is a way to keep our bodies strong against disease?
questions.ruby_prompt: Healthy bodies fight illness better. Which one keeps us strong?
options: Healthy food, exercise, enough sleep and clean water
questions.expected: Healthy food, exercise, enough sleep and clean water
questions.memo: A healthy lifestyle is the body's first defence. Good food, movement, sleep and clean water all keep your immune system ready.

questions.question: Put these steps for visiting a sick family member in order.
questions.ruby_prompt: When a family member is sick, what is a kind, safe way to be with them? Put steps in order.
options: Sit quietly and ask how they feel
Bring them water or something they can have
Wash your hands again when you leave
questions.expected: Wash your hands before entering,Sit quietly and ask how they feel,Bring them water or something they can have,Wash your hands again when you leave
questions.memo: Hands clean coming in, kindness while you are there, hands clean going out. Simple steps protect them and you.

questions.question: Why is it kind to listen to a friend talk about a person they have lost?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is it kind to listen when a friend talks about someone they have lost?
options: Talking about people we love helps us remember and heal
questions.expected: Talking about people we love helps us remember and heal
questions.memo: Sharing memories keeps people in our hearts. A good friend listens without trying to fix the sadness.

questions.question: If a friend tells you they are very, very sad and don't want to be here, who should you tell?
questions.ruby_prompt: A friend says they are so sad they don't want to be here anymore. This is serious — who should you tell?
options: A trusted grown-up immediately — a parent, teacher, or counsellor
questions.expected: A trusted grown-up immediately — a parent, teacher, or counsellor
questions.memo: When a friend is in serious pain, telling a trusted grown-up right away is the kindest, bravest thing. It is never telling tales — it is saving a life. SADAG (0800 567 567) helps too.

LS.L3.BKH.T06.title: Famous places in South Africa
LS.L3.BKH.T06.description: Local famous places, SA heritage sites, locating places on a map, safety in public.
LS.L3.BKH.T06.recovery_strategy: Use a simple SA map on the wall and put a sticker on each place you discuss. Real geography sticks when you can see where places sit on the map.

questions.question: Which city is at the southern tip of South Africa, near Table Mountain?
questions.ruby_prompt: South Africa's famous mountain city. Which one?
questions.expected: Cape Town
questions.memo: Cape Town is at the southern tip of SA, with the famous flat-topped Table Mountain rising above it.

questions.question: Which is South Africa's biggest game reserve?
questions.ruby_prompt: South Africa has many game reserves. Which is the biggest and most famous?
questions.expected: Kruger National Park
questions.memo: The Kruger National Park is one of Africa's largest game reserves. People come from all over the world to see the Big Five there.

questions.question: What is the Union Buildings used for?
questions.ruby_prompt: The Union Buildings in Pretoria are very important. What are they used for?
options: The government offices of the President
questions.expected: The government offices of the President
questions.memo: The Union Buildings in Pretoria are where the President of South Africa works. Nelson Mandela was inaugurated there in 1994.

questions.question: Robben Island is famous because Nelson Mandela was imprisoned there.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Robben Island is famous because Nelson Mandela was imprisoned there.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — Nelson Mandela was held on Robben Island for many years during apartheid. Today it is a museum that visitors can tour.

questions.question: Which mountain range stretches across the eastern side of South Africa?
questions.ruby_prompt: There is a big mountain range on SA's eastern side. Which one?
questions.expected: The Drakensberg
questions.memo: The Drakensberg is a huge mountain range running through KwaZulu-Natal, Free State and the Eastern Cape. It even has snow in winter.

questions.question: Which is South Africa's biggest city?
questions.ruby_prompt: South Africa's biggest city is the centre of business in the country. Which is it?
questions.expected: Johannesburg
questions.memo: Johannesburg is South Africa's biggest city. It grew up around gold mining and is the financial heart of the country.

questions.question: Which one is a place on a map showing where Cape Town sits?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one shows Cape Town's location?
questions.context: Picture: a dot in the south-west corner of South Africa, a dot in the middle, a dot in the north-east, a dot outside Africa.
options: A dot in the south-west corner of South Africa
A dot in the middle of the country
questions.expected: A dot in the south-west corner of South Africa
questions.memo: Cape Town is in the south-west, where two oceans meet. Learning to read a map helps you find places.

questions.question: Why must we stay close to a grown-up in a busy public place like a market?
questions.ruby_prompt: In a busy market or mall, why is it important to stay close to a grown-up?
options: So we don't get lost or in danger
questions.expected: So we don't get lost or in danger
questions.memo: Busy places have many people moving fast. Staying close to a grown-up means you don't get separated or approached by strangers.

questions.question: What is a 'heritage site'?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some places are called heritage sites. What does that mean?
options: A place protected because of its special history or natural beauty
questions.expected: A place protected because of its special history or natural beauty
questions.memo: Heritage sites tell us about the past or protect special natural spaces. Robben Island and the Cradle of Humankind are both heritage sites.

questions.question: Tell me about one famous place in South Africa you would like to visit, and why.
questions.ruby_prompt: South Africa has many lovely places. Tell me one you would like to visit and why.
questions.expected: I would like to visit the Kruger Park to see elephants
questions.memo: Any answer counts — Cape Town, Kruger, Robben Island, the Drakensberg, a local landmark in your town. Saying why helps you think about what interests you.

questions.question: Why is the Cradle of Humankind a special place?
questions.ruby_prompt: Near Johannesburg there is a place called the Cradle of Humankind. Why is it special?
options: Very old human ancestor fossils have been found there
It is the smallest place in SA
questions.expected: Very old human ancestor fossils have been found there
questions.memo: The Cradle of Humankind has caves where some of the oldest human ancestor fossils were found. It is a World Heritage Site.

questions.question: If you get lost in a shopping mall, what is the safest thing to do?
questions.ruby_prompt: You're at a mall and can't find your family. What is the safest thing to do?
options: Go to a security guard or shop helper in uniform and ask for help
questions.expected: Go to a security guard or shop helper in uniform and ask for help
questions.memo: Security and shop staff are trained to help lost children. They have ways to find your family quickly. Never leave with a stranger.

questions.question: Which one is a beach city in South Africa?
questions.ruby_prompt: SA has cities on the coast with lovely beaches. Which one is a beach city?
questions.expected: Durban
questions.memo: Durban is on the east coast and has warm beaches. Cape Town and Port Elizabeth (Gqeberha) also have beaches, but Durban is famous for them.

questions.question: Why must we not climb over fences at game reserves?
questions.ruby_prompt: Game reserve fences must always be respected. Why?
options: Wild animals can be dangerous and the fences keep us safe
questions.expected: Wild animals can be dangerous and the fences keep us safe
questions.memo: Fences protect us from wild animals and protect animals from us. Stay in safe viewing areas at all times.

questions.question: What is the Voortrekker Monument?
questions.ruby_prompt: Pretoria has a famous monument on a hill. What is the Voortrekker Monument?
options: A monument remembering the Voortrekkers' Great Trek into the interior
questions.expected: A monument remembering the Voortrekkers' Great Trek into the interior
questions.memo: The Voortrekker Monument remembers the Voortrekkers who moved inland from the Cape in the 1800s. It is part of South Africa's complex history.

questions.question: Put these South African cities in order from south to north.
questions.ruby_prompt: These four SA cities are at different parts of the country. Put them in order from south to north.
questions.expected: Cape Town,Bloemfontein,Johannesburg,Polokwane
questions.memo: Cape Town is at the very south. Bloemfontein is in the middle. Johannesburg is north of that, and Polokwane is in the far north of SA.

questions.question: Why is Table Mountain a special natural place?
questions.ruby_prompt: Table Mountain is one of SA's most famous landmarks. Why is it special?
options: Its flat top, ancient age, and rare fynbos plants
questions.expected: Its flat top, ancient age, and rare fynbos plants
questions.memo: Table Mountain is over 500 million years old. It has a unique flat top and home to plants that grow nowhere else on Earth.

questions.question: Most South Africans live in cities, not in rural areas.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Most South Africans today live in cities, not in rural areas.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — over time, more people have moved to cities for work and schooling. But many families still keep links with rural family homes.

questions.question: What can you do at a museum?
questions.ruby_prompt: Museums are special places. What can you do there?
options: Look at and learn about old or interesting things
questions.expected: Look at and learn about old or interesting things
questions.memo: Museums show us history, art, science and culture. We use quiet voices and look without touching unless a sign says otherwise.

questions.question: Name a famous place near where you live and tell me one thing about it.
questions.ruby_prompt: Every area has its famous spots. Tell me about one near you and one thing about it.
questions.expected: Our local park is famous for its big old trees
questions.memo: Any local landmark counts — a market, monument, church, park, sports stadium. Knowing your area builds a sense of belonging.

LS.L3.BKH.T07.title: Stories from key South African historical events
LS.L3.BKH.T07.description: Family history, simple time line, events affecting SA communities, phrases for passing time (before/after/long ago).
LS.L3.BKH.T07.recovery_strategy: Connect history to family stories the learner already knows. Big events feel real when grandparents lived through them.

questions.question: Who became South Africa's first democratically elected president in 1994?
questions.ruby_prompt: South Africa became a free democracy in 1994. Who was our first president after that?
questions.expected: Nelson Mandela
questions.memo: Nelson Mandela became South Africa's first black president in 1994 after democratic elections that everyone could vote in. It changed the country forever.

questions.question: What was apartheid?
questions.ruby_prompt: We hear the word apartheid in our history. What was it?
options: A system that unfairly separated people by race
questions.expected: A system that unfairly separated people by race
questions.memo: Apartheid was a system from 1948 to 1994 that gave different rights to different races. The struggle to end it shaped modern South Africa.

questions.question: When does South Africa celebrate Freedom Day?
questions.ruby_prompt: Freedom Day is when we remember our first democratic election. Which month is it in?
questions.expected: April
questions.memo: Freedom Day is on 27 April. It marks the day in 1994 when all South Africans could vote in elections for the first time.

questions.question: What does 'long ago' mean?
questions.ruby_prompt: We use the phrase 'long ago' in stories. What does it mean?
options: A time in the past, often many years before now
questions.expected: A time in the past, often many years before now
questions.memo: 'Long ago' points back in time — to your grandparents' childhoods, or even further. History uses words like long ago, in the past, and before.

questions.question: What is a 'time line'?
questions.ruby_prompt: We sometimes draw a time line. What is one?
options: A line showing when events happened in order
questions.expected: A line showing when events happened in order
questions.memo: Time lines put events in the order they happened. You can make one for your own life — birth, starting school, key moments.

questions.question: Put these moments in your life in order, from earliest to most recent.
questions.ruby_prompt: Imagine a time line of your life. Put these in order from earliest to latest.
options: You started Grade R or pre-school
questions.expected: You were born,You learnt to walk,You started Grade R or pre-school,You are now in Grade 3
questions.memo: Your life has a time line too. We are born, we grow, we learn — these events follow one another.

questions.question: Who was King Shaka?
questions.ruby_prompt: King Shaka is a very important figure in SA history. Who was he?
options: A powerful Zulu king who lived in the 1800s
A president of SA in modern times
questions.expected: A powerful Zulu king who lived in the 1800s
questions.memo: King Shaka led the Zulu people in the early 1800s. He was a strong leader and warrior, and remembered as an important figure in SA history.

questions.question: What happened in Soweto on 16 June 1976?
questions.ruby_prompt: On 16 June each year, we have Youth Day. What happened on 16 June 1976?
options: School learners protested for better education and many were hurt or killed
questions.expected: School learners protested for better education and many were hurt or killed
questions.memo: On 16 June 1976, schoolchildren in Soweto marched to protest unfair education laws. Many were hurt or killed. Today we remember them on Youth Day.

questions.question: Why is it important to remember difficult events from our history?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some history is sad or painful. Why do we still talk about it?
options: So we can learn from the past and not repeat mistakes
questions.expected: So we can learn from the past and not repeat mistakes
questions.memo: Knowing the past helps us understand today and build a fairer tomorrow. We honour those who suffered by remembering.

questions.question: Which is a way you can find out about your family's history?
questions.ruby_prompt: How can you learn about your own family's past?
options: Ask grandparents and older relatives to share stories
questions.expected: Ask grandparents and older relatives to share stories
questions.memo: Elders carry family history in their memory. Asking them — and listening — keeps the stories alive for the next generation.

questions.question: Long ago, what was used to write before there was paper?
questions.ruby_prompt: Before paper was common, what was used to write on?
options: Animal skins, papyrus, stone tablets and wax
questions.expected: Animal skins, papyrus, stone tablets and wax
questions.memo: Different cultures used what they had — papyrus reeds in Egypt, animal skins in Europe, clay tablets in the Middle East. Paper came much later.

questions.question: What does 'in the past' mean?
questions.ruby_prompt: When we say 'in the past', what do we mean?
options: A time before now — events that have already happened
questions.expected: A time before now — events that have already happened
questions.memo: 'In the past' means anything that has already happened, from one minute ago to thousands of years back.

questions.question: Tell me one event from your own life that you remember well.
questions.ruby_prompt: Everyone has memorable moments. Tell me one event from your life you remember well.
questions.expected: The day my baby sister was born
questions.memo: Family events, school days, holidays, special birthdays — all are part of your personal history. Any answer counts.

questions.question: What is the meaning of Heritage Day in South Africa?
questions.ruby_prompt: On 24 September we celebrate Heritage Day. What is the meaning of it?
options: We celebrate the cultures, foods and traditions of all South Africans
questions.expected: We celebrate the cultures, foods and traditions of all South Africans
questions.memo: Heritage Day is a chance for everyone to share their culture — clothes, food, songs, languages. Many families have a braai together.

questions.question: South Africa became a democracy in 1994.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? South Africa became a democracy in 1994.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — in 1994 South Africa held its first elections where all adults could vote, regardless of race. That marked the start of our democracy.

questions.question: Which one happened first in South African history?
questions.ruby_prompt: Two events from SA history. Which one came first?
options: Nelson Mandela's release from prison in 1990
questions.expected: The Soweto Uprising in 1976
questions.memo: The Soweto Uprising happened in 1976. Nelson Mandela was released from prison many years later, in 1990. 1976 came first.

questions.question: What is a 'history book'?
questions.ruby_prompt: We sometimes read history books at school. What is one?
options: A book that tells about events from the past
questions.expected: A book that tells about events from the past
questions.memo: History books gather knowledge about what happened long ago. They use evidence — letters, photos, artefacts — to tell the story.

questions.question: Why is it kind to listen to elders share their stories?
questions.ruby_prompt: Elders have many stories to share. Why is it kind to listen?
options: We learn from them and they feel respected and remembered
We just have to wait until they finish
questions.expected: We learn from them and they feel respected and remembered
questions.memo: Listening to elders is one of the most important things we can do. Their stories are gifts — and they help us know who we are.

questions.question: Name one event in your family's history that is important to your family.
questions.ruby_prompt: Family histories include big moments. Name one event that matters to your family.
questions.expected: When my grandparents got married
questions.memo: Births, weddings, moves, achievements, hard times shared — every family has its key events. They make us who we are.

questions.question: Why do we use words like 'before' and 'after' when telling history?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why do we use words like 'before' and 'after' when we talk about history?
options: They help us understand the order in which events happened
questions.expected: They help us understand the order in which events happened
questions.memo: Time words let us see cause and effect — what came before led to what came after. Order is part of understanding history.

LS.L3.BKH.T08.title: Pollution and recycling
LS.L3.BKH.T08.description: Types of pollution (water/air/land), effects on humans and environment, recycling, recyclable waste, illnesses from pollution.
LS.L3.BKH.T08.recovery_strategy: Pick one piece of litter near where you teach. Talk about it: where did it come from, where will it end up. Concrete examples beat abstract pollution talk.

questions.question: What is 'pollution'?
questions.ruby_prompt: We hear the word 'pollution' a lot. What does it mean?
options: Harmful waste or chemicals in the air, water, or land
questions.expected: Harmful waste or chemicals in the air, water, or land
questions.memo: Pollution is when waste and chemicals harm the environment. It can be in the air we breathe, water we drink, or land we live on.

questions.question: Which one is air pollution?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one is air pollution?
questions.context: Picture: smoke from a factory chimney, a clean blue sky, fresh air over a field, a tree in spring.
questions.expected: Smoke from a factory chimney
questions.memo: Factory smoke fills the air with poisons. Clean air is what we want to breathe, but pollution makes air harder on our lungs.

questions.question: What is 'recycling'?
questions.ruby_prompt: Recycling is something we hear about often. What is it?
options: Using old materials to make something new
questions.expected: Using old materials to make something new
questions.memo: Recycling turns used items into new ones. Glass becomes new glass, paper becomes new paper, plastic becomes new plastic. Less waste, less pollution.

questions.question: Which is something we can recycle at home?
questions.ruby_prompt: Lots of things from home can be recycled. Which one?
questions.expected: Empty glass and plastic bottles
questions.memo: Bottles can be washed and recycled. Rotten food belongs in compost, tissues and rags usually in the regular bin.

questions.question: Why is plastic in the ocean a big problem?
questions.ruby_prompt: Plastic in the ocean is a serious worry. Why?
options: Sea animals eat it and get sick or die
Fish like to swim through it
Plastic dissolves and helps the sea
questions.expected: Sea animals eat it and get sick or die
questions.memo: Sea turtles, fish, birds and whales mistake plastic for food. Plastic also breaks into tiny pieces that fish swallow. Less plastic helps protect them.

questions.question: What is a 'landfill'?
questions.ruby_prompt: Our rubbish goes to a place called a landfill. What is one?
options: A large area where rubbish is dumped and buried
questions.expected: A large area where rubbish is dumped and buried
questions.memo: Landfills are huge dump sites. The more we recycle, the less goes to landfill, and the less harmful pollution leaks into the soil and water.

questions.question: Put these recycling steps in order.
questions.ruby_prompt: Recycling at home has a few steps. Put them in order.
options: Sort waste by type (glass, plastic, paper)
Put each type in the right bin
Take to a recycling collection point
questions.expected: Sort waste by type (glass, plastic, paper),Rinse food off recyclables,Put each type in the right bin,Take to a recycling collection point
questions.memo: Sorting first means each material can be reused. Rinsing helps with contamination. Then proper bins, then collection.

questions.question: Burning waste at home can harm health.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Burning waste at home (especially plastic) can harm people's health.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — burning plastic releases poisons into the air that can cause coughs and serious lung problems, especially for children.

questions.question: Which one is water pollution?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one shows water pollution?
questions.context: Picture: a river with oil and plastic floating on top, a clean stream, a swimming pool, a glass of clean water.
options: A river with oil and plastic floating on top
questions.expected: A river with oil and plastic floating on top
questions.memo: Water pollution can be oil, plastic, sewage, or chemicals in rivers, dams or the sea. It harms fish and the people who drink the water.

questions.question: Name one way you and your family can reduce waste at home.
questions.ruby_prompt: Reducing waste helps the planet. Name one way you and your family can do less waste.
questions.expected: Reuse plastic shopping bags
questions.memo: Many ideas — reuse bottles, compost food scraps, buy fewer disposable items, take cloth bags shopping, fix instead of throw away. All count.

questions.question: Why is dropping litter on the ground a problem?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is dropping litter on the ground a big problem?
options: It makes places dirty, harms animals and can end up in our water
questions.expected: It makes places dirty, harms animals and can end up in our water
questions.memo: Litter blows into rivers, hurts animals, and makes our towns ugly. Using bins keeps the place healthy for everyone.

questions.question: What can old food scraps become if we compost them?
questions.ruby_prompt: Food scraps don't have to go in the bin. What can they become?
options: Compost — rich soil that helps plants grow
questions.expected: Compost — rich soil that helps plants grow
questions.memo: Composting turns peelings, leaves and eggshells into rich soil. Many schools and homes have compost heaps for their gardens.

questions.question: What is 'land pollution'?
questions.ruby_prompt: Land pollution is one type of pollution. What is it?
options: Harmful waste and chemicals making the soil dirty
questions.expected: Harmful waste and chemicals making the soil dirty
questions.memo: Land pollution happens when chemicals from rubbish leak into the soil. It can make food and water grown there unsafe.

questions.question: Why is it important to use both sides of a piece of paper?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why might it be good to use both sides of a piece of paper?
options: Paper is made from trees — using both sides saves trees
questions.expected: Paper is made from trees — using both sides saves trees
questions.memo: Trees take many years to grow. Using paper carefully — both sides, recycling it after — keeps forests alive.

questions.question: Cars and taxis can cause air pollution.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Cars and taxis can cause air pollution.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — petrol and diesel engines release exhaust gases that pollute the air. Walking, cycling and public transport reduce this.

questions.question: Which one is a recycling project at school?
questions.ruby_prompt: Schools can do recycling projects. Which one is a school recycling idea?
options: A bin for paper and another for plastic in every classroom
Throwing all rubbish in the school yard
questions.expected: A bin for paper and another for plastic in every classroom
questions.memo: Sorting bins at school teach habits. When learners get used to it, they bring those habits home.

questions.question: What can dirty air do to people's health?
questions.ruby_prompt: When the air is full of pollution, what can it do to people's health?
options: Cause coughs, asthma and long-term lung problems
questions.expected: Cause coughs, asthma and long-term lung problems
questions.memo: Polluted air harms lungs, especially for children and elders. That is why reducing pollution helps everyone's health.

questions.question: Which one is a renewable, cleaner source of energy?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some energy sources cause less pollution. Which is cleaner and renewable?
questions.expected: Solar (sun) power
questions.memo: Solar power uses sunshine, which never runs out and makes no smoke. Coal and oil pollute when they burn.

questions.question: Tell me one thing your school could do to be more eco-friendly.
questions.ruby_prompt: Imagine your school becoming more eco-friendly. Name one thing it could do.
questions.expected: Start a vegetable garden using compost from food scraps
questions.memo: Many ideas count — recycling bins, a vegetable garden, planting trees, saving water in tank, walking days. The point is action.

questions.question: Why is reducing waste even better than recycling it?
questions.ruby_prompt: Recycling is good, but reducing waste in the first place is even better. Why?
options: Less waste means less energy to recycle and less pollution overall
questions.expected: Less waste means less energy to recycle and less pollution overall
questions.memo: The 'three Rs' have an order — Reduce, Reuse, Recycle. Cutting waste at the start has the biggest impact on the environment.

LS.L3.BKH.T09.title: Natural disasters
LS.L3.BKH.T09.description: Severe weather experiences, natural disasters and their results, climatic changes (global warming), water-borne diseases.
LS.L3.BKH.T09.recovery_strategy: Anchor disaster talk to weather events the learner knows — a big storm, a flood on the way to school. Real experience makes vocabulary stick, while emphasising that grown-ups and emergency services help when disasters happen.

questions.question: What is a 'natural disaster'?
questions.ruby_prompt: We hear the words 'natural disaster' in the news. What is one?
options: A big harmful event from nature — like a flood, storm, or earthquake
questions.expected: A big harmful event from nature — like a flood, storm, or earthquake
questions.memo: Natural disasters are powerful events from nature that can harm people, animals and property. Communities and emergency services work together to recover.

questions.question: Which is a natural disaster that happens often in South Africa?
questions.ruby_prompt: South Africa has its own natural disasters. Which one is common here?
options: Drought (long dry periods with too little rain)
questions.expected: Drought (long dry periods with too little rain)
questions.memo: Many parts of SA have suffered drought, especially the Western Cape and Northern Cape. Drought affects farming, drinking water, and food prices.

questions.question: What should you do during a thunderstorm with lightning?
questions.ruby_prompt: There is loud thunder and lightning outside. What is the safest thing to do?
options: Stay inside, away from windows and open doors
Stand in the middle of a sports field
questions.expected: Stay inside, away from windows and open doors
questions.memo: Lightning is very dangerous. Tall trees, open spaces and metal objects all attract it. Inside, away from windows, is safest.

questions.question: What is a 'flood'?
questions.ruby_prompt: We hear of floods after heavy rain. What is a flood?
options: When water rises over land that is usually dry
questions.expected: When water rises over land that is usually dry
questions.memo: Floods happen when too much water — from rain or a river — covers areas where people live. Floods can damage homes and roads quickly.

questions.question: What does 'global warming' mean?
questions.ruby_prompt: Scientists talk about 'global warming'. What does it mean?
options: The Earth getting slowly warmer, causing more severe weather
questions.expected: The Earth getting slowly warmer, causing more severe weather
questions.memo: Earth's average temperature is rising because of gases from cars, factories and farms. Warmer weather can mean more droughts, storms and floods.

questions.question: Why must we never walk through floodwater?
questions.ruby_prompt: After heavy rain, water might cover the road. Why must we never walk through it?
options: It can be deeper, faster, and dirtier than it looks
It is safe if you are barefoot
questions.expected: It can be deeper, faster, and dirtier than it looks
questions.memo: Floods can hide deep holes, fast currents, and dangerous germs. Even a few centimetres of fast-moving water can knock you off your feet.

questions.question: Which one is a sign of a wildfire?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one is a sign of a wildfire?
questions.context: Picture: thick smoke rising over hills, a clear sunset, a foggy morning, fireworks at night.
questions.expected: Thick smoke rising over hills
questions.memo: Wildfires send up large clouds of smoke. If you see this in nature areas, alert a grown-up to call emergency services immediately.

questions.question: Why do we need an emergency family plan?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some families make a plan for emergencies. Why?
options: So everyone knows what to do and where to meet if disaster happens
questions.expected: So everyone knows what to do and where to meet if disaster happens
questions.memo: Planning ahead — meeting place, key phone numbers, what to grab — helps families stay safe and together when emergencies happen.

questions.question: Cholera and other water-borne diseases can spread after a flood.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Cholera and other water-borne diseases can spread after a flood.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — floodwater mixes with sewage, contaminating drinking water. After floods, clean water and good hygiene matter even more.

questions.question: Tell me about a time you experienced bad weather and what your family did.
questions.ruby_prompt: Bad weather affects all of us. Tell me about a time and what your family did to stay safe.
questions.expected: When a big storm came, we stayed inside and lit candles
questions.memo: Storms, hail, heavy rain, even a power cut — sharing helps you remember that families and communities cope together.

questions.question: What is an 'earthquake'?
questions.ruby_prompt: An earthquake is a kind of natural disaster. What is it?
options: The ground shaking because of movement deep inside the Earth
questions.expected: The ground shaking because of movement deep inside the Earth
questions.memo: The Earth's outer layer is made of huge pieces called plates. When they move suddenly, the ground shakes — an earthquake. SA gets small ones sometimes.

questions.question: Why do people plant trees to help fight climate change?
questions.ruby_prompt: Many groups plant trees to fight climate change. Why does this help?
options: Trees take in carbon dioxide and clean the air
questions.expected: Trees take in carbon dioxide and clean the air
questions.memo: Trees breathe in the gases that warm the planet and breathe out oxygen for us. More trees means cleaner air and a cooler planet.

questions.question: Who helps after a big natural disaster?
questions.ruby_prompt: After a disaster like a flood, who comes to help?
options: Police, fire fighters, doctors, NGOs and government services
questions.expected: Police, fire fighters, doctors, NGOs and government services
questions.memo: Big disasters bring many helpers — police, firefighters, paramedics, the Red Cross, charities and government. Many people work together.

questions.question: What is 'load-shedding' in South Africa?
questions.ruby_prompt: We hear about load-shedding in SA. What is it?
options: When power is switched off for hours to save the electricity grid
questions.expected: When power is switched off for hours to save the electricity grid
questions.memo: Load-shedding is when Eskom cuts power in turns so the whole grid doesn't crash. Families plan around the schedule with candles, batteries or gas stoves.

questions.question: Put these flood safety steps in order.
questions.ruby_prompt: Floods can happen quickly. Put these safety steps in order.
options: Listen to grown-ups and emergency services
Drink only clean, bottled or boiled water
questions.expected: Move to high ground,Avoid walking through floodwater,Listen to grown-ups and emergency services,Drink only clean, bottled or boiled water
questions.memo: First get safe — high ground. Then stay safe — no walking through water. Then follow instructions. Then keep healthy with clean water.

questions.question: Why might one community use less water during drought?
questions.ruby_prompt: During drought, families use less water. Why?
options: To save the limited water for everyone in the community
questions.expected: To save the limited water for everyone in the community
questions.memo: Drought means less water for drinking, cooking and farming. Every family using less means there is enough to share.

questions.question: Which one is something children can do to help during a small natural disaster like a storm?
questions.ruby_prompt: Children can help in small ways during disasters. Which one is a helpful action?
options: Stay calm, listen to grown-ups, and help younger siblings stay calm
questions.expected: Stay calm, listen to grown-ups, and help younger siblings stay calm
questions.memo: Staying calm helps everyone. Helping younger siblings, doing what grown-ups ask — these small actions matter.

questions.question: What happens when there is a hailstorm?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some storms drop hail. What is hail?
options: Balls of ice that fall from the sky
questions.expected: Balls of ice that fall from the sky
questions.memo: Hail forms high in storm clouds when raindrops are pushed up into very cold air and freeze. Big hail can break windows and dent cars.

questions.question: Name one way climate change might affect South Africa.
questions.ruby_prompt: Climate change has effects in South Africa. Name one.
questions.expected: More droughts and water shortages
questions.memo: Possible answers — more droughts, more severe storms, hotter summers, fires, less water for farming. Many right answers.

questions.question: If you smell gas in your home, what should you do?
questions.ruby_prompt: You smell gas at home. What should you do first?
options: Tell a grown-up and open windows — don't light matches or switches
Light a candle to see better
Run a hot stove to heat the room
questions.expected: Tell a grown-up and open windows — don't light matches or switches
questions.memo: Gas leaks can explode if there is a spark. Even turning on a light switch can cause one. Always tell a grown-up first.

LS.L3.BKH.T10.title: Stories of role models from different cultures
LS.L3.BKH.T10.description: Family/community role models, characteristics of a good role model, diversity of role models, contributions to medicine/sports/literature.
LS.L3.BKH.T10.recovery_strategy: Let learners choose role models from their own world first — a parent, gogo, sports coach, neighbour. Role models don't need to be famous. Affirm every choice.

questions.question: What is a 'role model'?
questions.ruby_prompt: We sometimes use the word 'role model'. What is a role model?
options: A person whose good actions inspire us
questions.expected: A person whose good actions inspire us
questions.memo: Role models can be anyone whose kindness, bravery or hard work shows us how to live well. They can be famous or just close to home.

questions.question: Which is a quality of a good role model?
questions.ruby_prompt: Role models share some qualities. Which one is a quality of a good role model?
questions.expected: Kindness, honesty and hard work
questions.memo: Role models inspire us by what they DO. Their kindness, honesty and effort show us how we might choose to act ourselves.

questions.question: Who is a famous South African doctor and freedom fighter?
questions.ruby_prompt: South Africa had many heroes who were doctors too. Who is a famous SA doctor and freedom fighter?
options: Dr Beyers Naudé or Dr Mamphela Ramphele
questions.expected: Dr Beyers Naudé or Dr Mamphela Ramphele
questions.memo: South Africa has produced many leaders who combined healing with fighting for fairness. Dr Mamphela Ramphele is a doctor, activist and businesswoman.

questions.question: Why is Siya Kolisi a sports role model?
questions.ruby_prompt: Siya Kolisi is famous in SA sport. Why is he a role model?
options: He overcame hard times to captain the Springboks to a Rugby World Cup
questions.expected: He overcame hard times to captain the Springboks to a Rugby World Cup
questions.memo: Siya Kolisi grew up with very little, but worked hard. He became the first black captain of the Springboks and led them to win the Rugby World Cup. Many SA children look up to him.

questions.question: A role model has to be famous.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? A role model has to be famous.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: No — your role model can be your gogo, your dad, a neighbour, a teacher. What matters is what they teach you by how they live.

questions.question: Tell me about one role model in your life and why.
questions.ruby_prompt: Many people inspire us. Tell me about one role model in your life and why.
questions.expected: My grandmother is my role model because she works hard and is always kind
questions.memo: Any answer counts — parents, grandparents, teachers, coaches, community workers. The 'why' matters more than the name.

questions.question: Who was the first black woman to be a justice on South Africa's highest court?
questions.ruby_prompt: There are many female SA role models. Who was the first black woman to be a justice on SA's highest court (Constitutional Court)?
questions.expected: Yvonne Mokgoro
questions.memo: Justice Yvonne Mokgoro was a pioneer — the first black female justice on SA's Constitutional Court. She helped shape our democracy.

questions.question: Why is it good to have role models from different cultures?
questions.ruby_prompt: Role models can come from any culture. Why is it good to have role models from many cultures?
options: It shows that any of us can do great things, whoever we are
questions.expected: It shows that any of us can do great things, whoever we are
questions.memo: Seeing role models from many cultures tells every child: people like me have done great things. That gives every child confidence.

questions.question: Which one is a way that a role model influences us?
questions.ruby_prompt: Role models change how we think and act. Which one is a way they influence us?
options: By showing what is possible through their actions
questions.expected: By showing what is possible through their actions
questions.memo: Role models inspire by example. When we see someone like us do something brave or kind, we believe we can too.

questions.question: Who was Albertina Sisulu?
questions.ruby_prompt: Albertina Sisulu is a famous SA role model. Who was she?
options: A nurse and freedom fighter known as the 'Mother of the Nation'
Just a character in a story
questions.expected: A nurse and freedom fighter known as the 'Mother of the Nation'
questions.memo: Albertina Sisulu was a nurse, a leader in the freedom struggle, and a quiet hero. Many people called her 'Mother of the Nation' for her unwavering courage.

questions.question: Which one shows a role model in everyday life?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one shows a role model in everyday life?
questions.context: Picture: a parent helping a child read, a person stealing, someone laughing at a younger child, someone breaking things.
options: A parent helping a child read
Someone laughing at a younger child
questions.expected: A parent helping a child read
questions.memo: Reading with a child shows patience and care — qualities of a role model. The other images show actions to avoid.

questions.question: Why do we sometimes need different role models for different parts of life?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why might we have different role models for sport, school, and family life?
options: Different people are good at different things — we learn from each
We only need one role model ever
questions.expected: Different people are good at different things — we learn from each
questions.memo: Your sports hero teaches discipline, your gogo teaches kindness, your teacher teaches curiosity. Each role model adds to who you become.

questions.question: What is the difference between admiring someone for what they have and what they do?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is the difference between admiring someone for what they have and what they do?
options: What people do is more meaningful — kindness lasts
questions.expected: What people do is more meaningful — kindness lasts
questions.memo: Role models are about actions and character, not possessions. Even people with very little can be the greatest role models.

questions.question: Charlize Theron is a famous South African in which industry?
questions.ruby_prompt: Charlize Theron is a SA-born star. In what industry is she famous?
questions.expected: Film and acting
questions.memo: Charlize Theron grew up in South Africa and became a famous actress in Hollywood. She also runs charities, especially for children with HIV.

questions.question: Caster Semenya is a famous role model in which sport?
questions.ruby_prompt: Caster Semenya is a SA sport hero. In which sport?
questions.expected: Middle-distance running
questions.memo: Caster Semenya won Olympic gold medals in middle-distance running. She has inspired many young South African athletes.

questions.question: How can you be a role model to younger children?
questions.ruby_prompt: Even at your age you can be a role model. How?
options: By being kind, helpful, and trying your best at things
questions.expected: By being kind, helpful, and trying your best at things
questions.memo: Younger children watch older ones. Your kindness and effort can teach them how to be — sometimes more than grown-ups' words can.

questions.question: Mamokgethi Phakeng is a role model in which field?
questions.ruby_prompt: Mamokgethi Phakeng is a SA role model in education. In what field?
questions.expected: Mathematics and science
questions.memo: Prof Phakeng is a top mathematician and former vice-chancellor of UCT. She inspires girls to pursue maths and science.

questions.question: Why is honesty a key quality in a role model?
questions.ruby_prompt: Honest people often become our role models. Why is honesty so important?
options: Honest people can be trusted, and trust is the base of every good relationship
Only adults need to be honest
questions.expected: Honest people can be trusted, and trust is the base of every good relationship
questions.memo: Without honesty, friendships, families and communities cannot work. That is why we look up to people who tell the truth, even when it is hard.

questions.question: Name one quality you would like to have when you grow up.
questions.ruby_prompt: Looking at your role models, name one quality you would like to have as you grow.
questions.expected: Patience like my mother has
questions.memo: Kindness, courage, patience, honesty, generosity — any quality you admire counts. Notice what your role models teach you.

questions.question: Role models are perfect and never make mistakes.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Role models are perfect and never make mistakes.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Nobody is perfect — role models included. What makes someone a role model is how they handle mistakes, apologise, and keep trying to do good.

LS.L3.BKH.T11.title: Understanding myself: my abilities, interests, rights and responsibilities
LS.L3.BKH.T11.description: Own abilities and interests, classmates' abilities, rights and responsibilities, classroom rules, health/safety responsibilities. SENSITIVE — self-esteem content.
LS.L3.BKH.T11.recovery_strategy: This topic is about self-esteem and rights. Reassure the learner that every child has unique strengths and equal rights. If they struggle to name an ability, point out one you've seen them do. Never let a learner feel small.

questions.question: What is an 'ability'?
questions.ruby_prompt: We use the word 'ability'. What does it mean?
options: Something you can do — a skill or strength
questions.expected: Something you can do — a skill or strength
questions.memo: Abilities are things you can do — running, drawing, reading, listening, making friends. Every person has different abilities, and that is good.

questions.question: Everyone has the same abilities and interests.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Everyone has the same abilities and interests.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: No — every person is different. Some love art, some love sport, some love numbers. Different abilities make our class and the world richer.

questions.question: Tell me one thing you are good at.
questions.ruby_prompt: Everyone is good at something. Tell me one thing you are good at.
questions.expected: I am good at running
questions.memo: Anything counts — running, drawing, helping younger siblings, being a kind friend, building things. Naming what you do well is a healthy thing.

questions.question: What is a 'right'?
questions.ruby_prompt: Children in South Africa have rights. What is a right?
options: Something every person should be able to have, like education or safety
questions.expected: Something every person should be able to have, like education or safety
questions.memo: Rights are things that protect us — to be safe, to learn, to be cared for. South Africa's Bill of Rights gives every child these protections.

questions.question: What is a 'responsibility'?
questions.ruby_prompt: Along with rights come responsibilities. What is a responsibility?
options: Something you are expected to do because it is important
questions.expected: Something you are expected to do because it is important
questions.memo: Responsibilities are things we take care of — like our homework, our family, our health. Doing them helps us and others.

questions.question: Which is a right that every child in South Africa has?
questions.ruby_prompt: South Africa's laws protect children. Which is a right every SA child has?
options: The right to go to school and be safe
The right to skip school all year
The right to eat only sweets
questions.expected: The right to go to school and be safe
questions.memo: All SA children have rights to education, safety, food, healthcare, and to be cared for. These are written in the Constitution.

questions.question: Which is a responsibility you have at home?
questions.ruby_prompt: Every child has responsibilities at home. Which is a common one?
options: Helping with small chores like tidying up
questions.expected: Helping with small chores like tidying up
questions.memo: Tidying your room, helping with washing, looking after younger siblings — these are responsibilities you can do. Grown-ups handle the big ones.

questions.question: Which is a responsibility you have at school?
questions.ruby_prompt: Schools depend on everyone doing their part. Which is a learner's responsibility at school?
options: Doing homework and listening to the teacher
questions.expected: Doing homework and listening to the teacher
questions.memo: Listening, doing homework, treating others kindly, looking after the school — these are responsibilities every learner has.

questions.question: Why are classroom rules important?
questions.ruby_prompt: Every class has rules. Why are they important?
options: Rules help everyone learn and feel safe
questions.expected: Rules help everyone learn and feel safe
questions.memo: Class rules — like 'one person speaks at a time' — let everyone learn together. Without them the noise would stop learning.

questions.question: Which is a classroom rule that helps everyone?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which rule helps everyone in the classroom?
questions.expected: Raise your hand to speak
questions.memo: Raising hands means the teacher can hear one person at a time, and everyone gets a chance to share.

questions.question: If a class votes on a new rule, what does that mean?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sometimes a class votes on a new rule. What does voting mean?
options: Each person says yes or no, and the majority decides
questions.expected: Each person says yes or no, and the majority decides
questions.memo: Voting is how democracies decide. In SA, adults vote for leaders. In class, voting lets everyone have a say.

questions.question: It is important to feel proud of your own abilities, even if they are different from your classmates'.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? It is important to feel proud of your own abilities, even if they are different from your classmates'.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — your abilities are yours. Comparing makes us feel small; celebrating ours makes us feel strong. Different is good.

questions.question: Why should we celebrate classmates who are good at different things than us?
questions.ruby_prompt: Our classmates are good at different things. Why should we celebrate that?
options: A class with many strengths can do more than a class where everyone is the same
questions.expected: A class with many strengths can do more than a class where everyone is the same
questions.memo: When different abilities work together, more becomes possible. A team needs runners and thinkers and helpers and creators.

questions.question: Which is a basic health responsibility you can do for yourself?
questions.ruby_prompt: Looking after our own health is one of our responsibilities. Which is one you can do?
options: Brush your teeth twice a day and eat well
questions.expected: Brush your teeth twice a day and eat well
questions.memo: Health responsibilities like brushing, washing, sleeping and eating well are things only YOU can do for your body. They are small but powerful.

questions.question: Tell me one interest of yours — something you enjoy doing.
questions.ruby_prompt: Interests are things we enjoy. Tell me one interest of yours.
questions.expected: I enjoy drawing pictures of animals
questions.memo: Reading, sport, music, drawing, helping at home, playing with friends — any interest is valid. Knowing what you enjoy helps you grow.

questions.question: What should you do if you see a classmate's right being broken — like being hurt by another child?
questions.ruby_prompt: If you see a classmate being hurt, what should you do?
options: Tell a teacher you trust so they can help
questions.expected: Tell a teacher you trust so they can help
questions.memo: Standing up for someone often means telling a trusted grown-up, not fighting back. Their right to safety matters as much as yours.

questions.question: Why does every child deserve to be treated with kindness?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why does every child deserve to be treated with kindness, no matter what?
