options: Because every child is a person with rights and feelings
questions.expected: Because every child is a person with rights and feelings
questions.memo: Every person has worth simply because they are a person. Wealth, looks, skills don't change that. Kindness for all is the rule.

questions.question: What can you do if you don't know how to do something but want to learn?
questions.ruby_prompt: If you don't know how to do something but want to learn it, what can you do?
options: Ask for help, practise, and keep trying
Decide you are bad at everything
questions.expected: Ask for help, practise, and keep trying
questions.memo: Learning new things takes time. Asking is brave. Practising is how everyone gets better. Patience with yourself matters.

questions.question: Put these classroom rule-making steps in order.
questions.ruby_prompt: Imagine the class is making a new rule together. Put the steps in order.
options: Discuss why each one might help
questions.expected: Suggest possible rules,Discuss why each one might help,Vote on which to keep,All follow the chosen rule
questions.memo: Good rule-making invites ideas, discussion, a vote, and everyone keeping the rule together. That's how democracy works.

questions.question: Name one responsibility you take seriously and why.
questions.ruby_prompt: We all have responsibilities. Name one you take seriously and tell me why.
questions.expected: I take care of my younger sister after school because she needs me
questions.memo: Any responsibility counts — homework, helping at home, caring for a pet, being a good friend. Saying 'why' shows you understand its meaning.

LS.L3.BKH.T12.title: Celebrations and festivals
LS.L3.BKH.T12.description: Religious and cultural celebrations, personal celebration experiences, traditional clothes, religious symbols and worship, places of worship, home safety measures.
LS.L3.BKH.T12.recovery_strategy: Celebrate the learner's own family traditions before introducing others. Respect every tradition — there are no 'right' or 'wrong' celebrations.

questions.question: What is a 'celebration'?
questions.ruby_prompt: Celebrations are special events. What is one?
options: A special event where people gather to mark something important
questions.expected: A special event where people gather to mark something important
questions.memo: Celebrations mark moments like birthdays, weddings, religious days or community wins. They bring people together with food, music and stories.

questions.question: When does South Africa celebrate Heritage Day?
questions.ruby_prompt: Heritage Day is one of our biggest celebrations. Which month is it in?
questions.expected: September (24 September)
questions.memo: Heritage Day is on 24 September. We celebrate all SA cultures, often with a braai and traditional clothes.

questions.question: What is 'Eid' in the Muslim community?
questions.ruby_prompt: Muslim families celebrate Eid. What is Eid?
options: A religious festival, often after a month of fasting (Ramadaan)
questions.expected: A religious festival, often after a month of fasting (Ramadaan)
questions.memo: Eid-ul-Fitr is celebrated after Ramadaan (a month when Muslims fast during the day). Families dress up, share meals, and visit each other.

questions.question: What is 'Diwali' in the Hindu community?
questions.ruby_prompt: Hindu families celebrate Diwali. What is it?
options: The festival of lights, celebrating good winning over evil
questions.expected: The festival of lights, celebrating good winning over evil
questions.memo: Diwali is celebrated with lights, sweets and family time. Many SA Hindu families light small clay lamps and share food.

questions.question: What is 'Christmas' in the Christian community?
questions.ruby_prompt: Many SA Christian families celebrate Christmas. What is it?
options: A celebration of the birth of Jesus, on 25 December
questions.expected: A celebration of the birth of Jesus, on 25 December
questions.memo: Christmas on 25 December is a Christian celebration of Jesus's birth. Many families share gifts, food and time together.

questions.question: Which is a place of worship for Christians?
questions.ruby_prompt: Different religions have different places of worship. What do Christians call theirs?
questions.expected: A church
questions.memo: Christians worship in churches. Muslims go to mosques, Hindus to temples (mandirs), and Jews to synagogues.

questions.question: Which is a place of worship for Muslims?
questions.ruby_prompt: Muslims pray at a special place. What is it called?
questions.expected: A mosque (also called masjid)
questions.memo: A mosque is where Muslims gather to pray. The big call to prayer (adhaan) sounds from a mosque five times a day.

questions.question: Which is a place of worship for Hindus?
questions.ruby_prompt: Hindus worship at a special building. What is it often called?
questions.expected: A temple (also called mandir)
questions.memo: Hindu temples are full of bright colours and statues of different gods. KZN has many beautiful old SA temples.

questions.question: Tell me about one celebration your family has each year.
questions.ruby_prompt: Every family has a special celebration. Tell me about one your family has each year.
questions.expected: We celebrate Christmas with a big family lunch
questions.memo: Birthdays, weddings, religious days, Heritage Day, family reunions — every celebration counts. Sharing yours helps others learn about your culture.

questions.question: Why is it kind to ask politely about a celebration you don't know?
questions.ruby_prompt: If a friend celebrates something you don't know, why is it kind to ask politely about it?
options: It shows respect and helps you understand their culture
questions.expected: It shows respect and helps you understand their culture
questions.memo: Asking with respect — not 'why do you do that weird thing' — is a kind way to learn. Most people are happy to share.

questions.question: Which is a traditional Zulu celebration outfit?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one is a traditional Zulu celebration outfit?
questions.context: Picture: a Zulu woman in a beaded isidwaba and traditional headpiece, a tracksuit, a swimming costume, a business suit.
options: A Zulu woman in a beaded isidwaba and traditional headpiece
questions.expected: A Zulu woman in a beaded isidwaba and traditional headpiece
questions.memo: Traditional Zulu clothing is rich with beadwork and meaning. Different colours and patterns mean different things — age, family, status.

questions.question: Which is a way many SA families celebrate Heritage Day?
questions.ruby_prompt: How do many SA families spend Heritage Day?
options: With a braai, traditional clothes, music and family
questions.expected: With a braai, traditional clothes, music and family
questions.memo: A braai (BBQ) is so common on Heritage Day that some people call it 'Braai Day'. It is also a chance to show traditional clothes and food.

questions.question: Why must we be safe when using fireworks during celebrations?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some celebrations use fireworks. Why must we be very safe with them?
options: Fireworks can burn or hurt people if not handled carefully
questions.expected: Fireworks can burn or hurt people if not handled carefully
questions.memo: Fireworks burn very hot and can blow up unexpectedly. Children should never light fireworks — only adults, and away from people, pets and houses.

questions.question: Different religions all deserve respect.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false? Different religions all deserve respect.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — South Africa is home to many faiths. All deserve respect. Our Constitution protects everyone's right to their own beliefs.

questions.question: What is the Jewish holiday of Pesach (Passover) about?
questions.ruby_prompt: Some SA families celebrate Pesach (Passover). What is it about?
options: Remembering the Jewish people's freedom from slavery in ancient Egypt
questions.expected: Remembering the Jewish people's freedom from slavery in ancient Egypt
questions.memo: Pesach is one of the most important Jewish festivals. Families share a special meal called a seder and tell the story of their ancestors' freedom.

questions.question: Why might families wear special clothes for a wedding?
questions.ruby_prompt: Weddings are special. Why do families often wear special clothes?
options: To honour the occasion and the couple getting married
questions.expected: To honour the occasion and the couple getting married
questions.memo: Special clothes show that an event is important. Many SA families combine traditional and modern wedding clothes in beautiful ways.

questions.question: Name one festival, holiday, or celebration that is important to your family or culture.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me about a festival, holiday or celebration that matters in your family or culture.
questions.expected: We celebrate Eid with our extended family every year
questions.memo: Any answer matters — Christmas, Eid, Diwali, a birthday, a wedding, Heritage Day. Sharing makes us closer.

questions.question: Which is a safety rule for home celebrations with many guests?
questions.ruby_prompt: When the home is full of guests for a celebration, which is a good safety rule?
options: Keep hot stoves and braais away from small children
Let small children climb on stoves
Lock all doors with people inside
questions.expected: Keep hot stoves and braais away from small children
questions.memo: Busy events mean grown-ups are distracted. Setting up safe spaces for small children — away from stoves, braais and pools — prevents accidents.

questions.question: Put these wedding celebration steps in a typical order.
questions.ruby_prompt: Many SA weddings have a typical order of events. Put them in order.
options: Family members arrive in traditional clothes
The ceremony where the couple makes promises
questions.expected: Family members arrive in traditional clothes,The ceremony where the couple makes promises,A special meal is shared,Music and dancing
questions.memo: Most weddings move from greetings, to the ceremony itself, to eating together, to celebrating with music and dance. Some details differ by culture.

questions.question: Why is it special when people from different cultures share each other's celebrations?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is it special when people from different cultures share each other's celebrations?
options: It builds friendship and shows that we are one community despite differences
questions.expected: It builds friendship and shows that we are one community despite differences
questions.memo: Sharing celebrations is one of the loveliest things in SA. A Christian friend at an Eid meal, a Hindu friend at a braai — these moments make us closer.
